definition_en: a flat round object, a disc that stores sound or data, or a pad between bones
core_image: 一片薄薄的圆盘在灯下转，边缘反出一圈白光
scene: 唱机的手臂落下，圆盘开始转，屋里响起沙沙的底噪。 He slid the disc into the player.
sceneCN: 这里 disc 指「光盘」（第 1 个义项：扁圆形的存储介质）；句意是他把光盘推进了播放机。

derivatives.zh: 迪斯科舞曲；迪斯科舞厅

senses.title: A round carrier of sound or data
senses.definition: a thin round object on which music or computer data is stored
senses.definitionCN: 存着音乐或电脑数据的薄圆片
senses.example: He slid the disc into the player.
senses.exampleCN: 他把光盘推进了播放机。
senses.why: A whole evening of sound hides in one shiny circle.
senses.whyCN: 一整个晚上的声音，藏在一个发亮的圆里。

senses.title: Any flat round object
senses.definition: a flat circular thing, such as a plate of metal
senses.definitionCN: 扁平的圆形物体，如一片金属盘
senses.example: The machine cuts a disc from the steel sheet.
senses.exampleCN: 机器从钢板上切下一个圆盘。
senses.why: The shape is older than any use people found for it.
senses.whyCN: 这个形状比人给它找的任何用途都更老。

senses.title: A pad between bones
senses.definition: a soft round pad that sits between the bones of the spine
senses.definitionCN: 夹在脊椎骨之间的软圆垫
senses.example: A damaged disc can press on a nerve.
senses.exampleCN: 受损的椎间盘会压到神经。
senses.why: Even the body keeps small round cushions between hard parts.
senses.whyCN: 连身体也要在硬骨之间垫上小圆垫。

intro.en: Disc goes back through Latin discus to Greek diskos, a flat round plate thrown in games.
intro.cn: disc 经拉丁语 discus 追溯到希腊语 diskos，指比赛中掷出的扁圆盘。

items.en: Diskos named a quoit, a flat stone or metal plate thrown in sport.
items.cn: diskos 指比赛里掷出的扁石盘或金属盘。

items.en: Discus borrowed the Greek word for the same object.
items.cn: discus 借来这个希腊词，指同样的东西。

items.en: Disc and disk entered English for a flat round surface.
items.cn: disc 与 disk 进入英语，指扁平的圆面。

items.en: Records and then compact discs gave the word a musical life.
items.cn: 唱片与后来的激光唱片，让这个词有了音乐的生命。

items.en: It now also names a cushion between spinal bones.
items.cn: 如今它也指脊椎骨之间的软垫。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the disc- shape, while the meaning group names other round flat things.
note.cn: 形近组共用 disc 这一形状词干，近义组则列出其他扁圆之物。

entries.definition: a flat round object or a computer storage device
a style of dance music with a strong beat
entries.definitionCN: 节奏强烈的迪斯科舞曲

entries.definition: a heavy disc thrown in an athletics event
entries.definitionCN: 田径比赛中掷出的重圆盘

entries.definition: a flat round dish used for food
a round plastic disc that carries recorded sound
entries.definitionCN: 录有声音的圆形塑料唱片

entries.definition: a large flat plate, or an old record disc

normalIntro.en: These hooks move from a spinning plate of sound to a soft pad inside the spine.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子从旋转的发声圆盘，走到脊椎里的软垫。

normal.en: Disc is a shape before it is a thing.
normal.cn: disc 先是一个形状，然后才是一件东西。

normal.en: A disc jockey turns two round plates into a night.
normal.cn: 唱片骑师把两张圆盘转成一个夜晚。

normal.en: Scratch a disc and the music stumbles.
normal.cn: 光盘一划伤，音乐就会打结。

normal.en: A slipped disc is a small cushion out of place.
normal.cn: 椎间盘突出，就是一个小软垫挪了位。

normal.en: The same round shape serves music, machines and the body.
normal.cn: 同一个圆形，服务音乐、机器与身体。

abstract.en: Picture a thin silver circle catching the light.
abstract.cn: 想象一个薄薄的银圆接住灯光。

abstract.en: Picture a needle settling into a groove.
abstract.cn: 想象唱针落进一道细槽。

abstract.en: Picture two bones with a soft round pad between them.
abstract.cn: 想象两块骨头之间垫着一个软圆垫。

examples.en: He slid the disc into the player.
examples.cn: 他把光盘推进了播放机。

examples.en: The disc was scratched and skipped.
examples.cn: 光盘划伤了，播放时跳音。

examples.en: The doctor found a damaged disc in her back.
examples.cn: 医生发现她背部有一处椎间盘受损。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 disc 记成「碟斯克」：碟子一样的圆片，就是 disc。

root: 来自希腊语 diskos（掷出的扁圆盘），经拉丁语 discus 进入英语，最初指扁平的圆面。后来唱片、激光光盘先后借用这个词，使它有了承载声音与数据的意思；医学上又用它指脊椎骨之间的软垫。

sensesIntro.en: From a shiny circle that holds music, to any flat round plate, to a cushion inside the spine.
sensesIntro.cn: 从装着音乐的亮圆片，到任何扁圆盘，再到脊椎里的软垫。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a thin round plate spinning under a light.
core.cn: 核心意象：一片薄圆盘在灯下旋转。

chain: DATA IS BURNED IN TINY DOTS
A SOFT PAD SITS BETWEEN BONES

branches.en: The first sense is the round carrier of sound or data.
branches.cn: 第一个义项是承载声音或数据的圆片。

branches.en: The second sense is the bare shape itself.
branches.cn: 第二个义项是那个形状本身。

branches.en: The third sense is the body's own small disc.
branches.cn: 第三个义项是身体里自带的小圆盘。

branches.en: Music and metal both borrow the same flat circle.
branches.cn: 音乐与金属借用了同一个扁圆。

branches.en: A pad between bones is a disc no one can see.
branches.cn: 骨间的软垫，是一只看不见的圆盘。

intro.en: Disc gathers a family of round and flat words, from disks to discus.
intro.cn: disc 聚起一族与圆、扁有关的词，从磁盘到铁饼。

latinIntro.en: Greek diskos and Latin discus, a thrown plate, give the base disc-.
latinIntro.cn: 希腊语 diskos 与拉丁语 discus（掷出的圆盘）给出词基 disc。

items.example: The disc lay face down on the desk.
items.exampleCN: 那张光盘正面朝下放在桌上。

items.meaning: a flat round object or storage device
items.example: The file is saved on the disk.
The party played disco all night.
items.exampleCN: 聚会整晚都在放迪斯科。

items.meaning: a heavy disc thrown in sport
items.example: He threw the discus across the field.

items.meaning: a person who plays recorded music
items.example: The disc jockey kept the crowd dancing.
items.exampleCN: 唱片骑师让全场一直跳着。

items.meaning: a machine part that reads discs
items.example: The disc drive would not open.

items.meaning: brakes that press on a round plate
items.example: The bike has disc brakes on both wheels.
items.exampleCN: 这辆车的两个轮子都装了盘式刹车。

items.meaning: having the form of a flat circle
items.example: The nest was disc-shaped and shallow.

definition_en: a fence or wall that stops movement, or something that blocks progress
core_image: 路边一排红白相间的隔离栏
scene: 人群被拦在警戒线外。 Police put a barrier across the road.
sceneCN: 这里 barrier 是「障碍物」（第 1 个义项：挡住通行的围栏或墙）；句意是警察在路上设了路障。

derivatives.zh: 同源基础词，义为「横木；栏杆」

senses.title: A fence that blocks
senses.definition: a fence, wall or object that stops people or vehicles
senses.definitionCN: 阻挡人或车辆通行的围栏、墙或物体
senses.example: Police put a barrier across the road.
senses.exampleCN: 警察在路上设了路障。
senses.why: Barrier came from Old French barriere, a fence made of bars, so it names a physical block.
senses.whyCN: barrier 来自古法语 barriere「用横木做的围栏」，所以它指实物的阻挡。

senses.title: Something that blocks progress
senses.definition: a problem or difference that prevents progress
senses.definitionCN: 阻碍进展的问题或差异
senses.example: Language is still a barrier for many newcomers.
senses.exampleCN: 语言仍是许多新来者的障碍。
senses.why: A fence in the way became a metaphor for anything that keeps people or progress apart.
senses.whyCN: 挡路的围栏被比作任何使人或进展受阻的东西。

intro.en: Barrier came from a French word for a fence of bars.
intro.cn: barrier 来自法语中表示「横木围栏」的词。

items.en: barre meant 'a bar or rod'.
items.cn: barre 意为「横木、杆」。

items.en: barriere meant 'a fence of bars'.
items.cn: barriere 意为「横木围栏」。

items.en: barrier named a defensive fence.
items.cn: barrier 指防御性围栏。

items.en: barrier covered abstract obstacles.
items.cn: barrier 扩展到抽象的障碍。

items.en: barrier is common in trade and language.
items.cn: 如今 barrier 常见于贸易与语言话题。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the barr- opening; the near-meaning group gives blocking things.
note.cn: 形近组都以 barr- 开头；近义组是阻挡物的说法。

a person who cuts hair
unable to produce plants
a barrier around a field
something that blocks progress
a solid barrier of brick or stone

normalIntro.en: A barrier is a row of bars that stops you.
normalIntro.cn: barrier 是一排挡住你的横木。

normal.en: The plural is barriers.
normal.cn: 复数是 barriers。

normal.en: A barrier to something blocks it.
normal.cn: a barrier to 表示某事的阻碍。

normal.en: Break down barriers means remove them.
normal.cn: break down barriers 意为消除隔阂。

normal.en: A language barrier is not physical.
normal.cn: language barrier 不是实物障碍。

normal.en: The stress is on the first syllable: BAR-rier.
normal.cn: 重音在第一音节。

abstract.en: See a wall of words between speakers.

examples.en: Police put a barrier across the road.
examples.cn: 警察在路上设了路障。

examples.cn: 语言仍是许多新来者的障碍。

examples.en: The crowd pressed against the barriers.

dict_mnemonic.text: bar（横木）加 -ier：一排横木立起来，就是挡路的 barrier。

root: 来自古法语 barriere，源于 barre「横木」；由用横木搭成的防御围栏，引申为任何阻挡通行或进展的障碍。

sensesIntro.en: A row of bars and an invisible gap both keep things apart.
sensesIntro.cn: 一排横木与一道看不见的缝隙，都把事情隔在两边。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: red and white rails across a road.

intro.en: The same bar base gives barricade, a temporary barrier.

latinIntro.en: There is no Latin base; the word came from Old French barriere.
latinIntro.cn: 这里没有拉丁词基，这个词来自古法语 barriere。

definition_en: a thin line where something has broken, or to break with a sharp sound
core_image: 冰面上出现一道细长的白痕，越裂越长
scene: 脚一踩，湖面的冰立刻裂开一道细长的白线。 The thin ice cracked under his boots.
sceneCN: 这里 crack 指「裂开」（第 2 个义项：因受力而出现裂缝）；句意是薄冰在他靴子下裂开了。

senses.title: A thin broken line
senses.definition: a thin line where something has broken but not fallen apart
senses.definitionCN: 物体破裂却还没散开时留下的细线
senses.example: There is a crack in the ceiling.
senses.exampleCN: 天花板上有一道裂缝。
senses.why: A hard thing gives a little, not all at once.
senses.whyCN: 硬东西会先让一点，不会一下子全碎。

senses.title: To break with a sound
senses.definition: to break with a sharp sound, or to develop a thin line
senses.definitionCN: 伴随脆响而破裂，或出现一道细纹
senses.example: The cup cracked when it hit the floor.
senses.exampleCN: 杯子砸到地上时裂了。
senses.why: Stone shouts when it finally gives way.
senses.whyCN: 石头最终让步时，会喊出一声。

senses.title: To solve something hard
senses.definition: to solve a difficult problem or a secret code
senses.definitionCN: 解决难题或破译秘密代码
senses.example: They cracked the code in one night.
senses.exampleCN: 他们一夜之间破解了密码。
senses.why: A hard shell must break before the kernel is reached.
senses.whyCN: 要吃到果仁，硬壳必须先破。

intro.en: Crack comes from Old English cracian, to make a sharp noise, a word shaped by the sound itself.
intro.cn: crack 源自古英语 cracian（发出脆响），这个词本身就是模仿声音造出来的。

items.en: Cracian meant to make a sharp noise.
items.cn: cracian 意为发出尖脆的声响。

items.en: Crack named the sound of something splitting.
items.cn: crack 指东西裂开时的响声。

items.en: It came to name the line left after the sound.
items.cn: 它接着用来指声音过后留下的那道线。

items.en: To crack a code borrowed the sense of breaking a shell.
items.cn: 「破解密码」借用了敲开外壳的意思。

items.en: It now covers cracks, jokes, codes and crackdowns.
items.cn: 今天它涵盖裂缝、笑话、密码与严厉打击。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers sharp-sounding words, and the meaning group names other kinds of break.
note.cn: 形近组收集带尖锐声响的词，近义组列出其他表示破裂的说法。

entries.definition: a loud violent collision
to make small repeated cracking sounds
to make a long high sound when moving
entries.definitionCN: 移动时发出又长又尖的响声

entries.definition: to divide along a line
a break in bone or hard material
an empty space between two things

normalIntro.en: These hooks start with a sharp sound, then move to the line it leaves and to a code broken open.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子从一声脆响开始，再到它留下的细线，最后到被敲开的密码。

normal.en: Say the word aloud: crack already sounds like breaking.
normal.cn: 把这词念出来，crack 本身就带着裂开的响声。

normal.en: A crack is the echo of a break frozen in place.
normal.cn: 裂缝就是一次断裂被冻住的回声。

normal.en: A cup cracks before it ever falls apart.
normal.cn: 杯子在彻底碎掉之前会先裂。

normal.en: To crack a code is to break its hard shell.
normal.cn: 破解密码，就是敲开它坚硬的外壳。

normal.en: A cracker is named for the sound it makes between your teeth.
normal.cn: 饼干的名字，来自它在牙间发出的那声脆响。

abstract.en: Picture a white line running across grey ice.
abstract.cn: 想象一道白线在灰冰上延伸。

abstract.en: Picture a hairline scar on a porcelain plate.
abstract.cn: 想象瓷盘上一道发丝般的裂痕。

abstract.en: Picture a locked box opening with a small snap.
abstract.cn: 想象一只锁着的箱子啪一声开了。

examples.en: A crack ran across the frozen pond.
examples.cn: 一道裂缝横穿结冰的池塘。

examples.en: The branch cracked under his weight.
examples.cn: 树枝在他的重量下裂了。

examples.en: She cracked two eggs into the pan.
examples.cn: 她把两个鸡蛋打进锅里。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 crack 记成「咔嚓」：东西裂开时那一声脆响，就是 crack，声音之后留下裂缝。

root: 源自古英语 cracian（发出脆响），是模拟声音构成的词，本指物体裂开时的声响，后指裂缝本身，又引申出破解与打击等义。

sensesIntro.en: From the sharp sound of breaking, to the line it leaves, to a hard problem solved.
sensesIntro.cn: 从破裂的脆响，到它留下的细线，最后到被解决的难题。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a white line splitting a hard surface.
core.cn: 核心意象：一道白线把硬表面劈开。

branches.en: The line stays because the two sides still hold.
branches.cn: 裂缝留下，是因为两边还撑着。

branches.en: The moment of breaking always makes a noise.
branches.cn: 破裂的那一刻总会发出一声。

branches.en: A secret is a shell, and solving it is cracking it open.
branches.cn: 秘密是一只壳，解开它就是把它敲开。

branches.en: Sound and line are two records of the same event.
branches.cn: 声音和细线，是同一件事的两份记录。

branches.en: Both a cup and a code can give way suddenly.
branches.cn: 杯子和密码都可能突然让步。

intro.en: Crack is an imitative base word that grows tools, actions and compounds with down and pot.
intro.cn: crack 是模拟声音的词根，可与表示工具、动作以及 down、pot 的词素组合。

latinIntro.en: There is no Latin source; the word is native English, shaped by sound.
latinIntro.cn: 它没有拉丁语来源，是英语本族词，由声音模仿而成。

items.meaning: a thin break or its sound
items.meaningCN: 细裂缝或它发出的响声

items.meaning: the act of breaking or solving
items.example: The cracking of the code took hours.
items.exampleCN: 破解密码花了几个小时。

items.example: He ate a cracker with cheese.
items.exampleCN: 他就着奶酪吃了一块饼干。

items.example: They called the inventor a crackpot.
items.exampleCN: 他们管那位发明家叫怪人。

definition_zh: 独一无二的；唯一的；独特的；极好的；罕见的
definition_en: being the only one of its kind, or unusually special and good
core_image: 一整块原石被凿成一只瓶，世上再没有第二只，连模具也没有留下来
scene: 博物馆的玻璃柜里放着一只烧坏的窑变瓷瓶，釉色在灯下像流动的水。 The curator says this unique piece cannot be copied, even by the same kiln.
sceneCN: 这里 unique 是「独一无二的」（第 1 个义项：同类中仅此一件）；句意为馆长说这件孤品即使同一座窑也复制不出来。柜中那只没有第二件的瓷瓶，就是这个词的样子。

derivatives.zh: 由本词加 -ly 构成，义为「独特地；唯一地」
由本词加 -ness 构成，义为「独特性；唯一性」
由本词加 -ity 构成，义为「唯一性」（较少用）

senses.title: The only one of its kind
senses.definition: existing as the single example of its kind, so that nothing else is the same
senses.definitionCN: 作为同类中的唯一存在，没有别的东西与它相同
senses.example: Each fingerprint is unique, even between identical twins.
senses.exampleCN: 每个指纹都是独一无二的，即使同卵双胞胎之间也不同。
senses.why: Latin unus means one: the word points to a class with only one member.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 unus 意为「一」：这个词所指的那一类里只有一名成员。

senses.title: Belonging to one thing only
senses.definition: belonging to or found in only one place, person, or group
senses.definitionCN: 只属于或只出现在某一个地方、人或群体
senses.example: This dialect is unique to a few fishing villages on the coast.
senses.exampleCN: 这种方言只存在于沿海几个渔村。
senses.why: Uniqueness can be claimed for a thing by pointing at the one place it occurs.
senses.whyCN: 只要指出它唯一出现的地方，就能为某物主张独有性。

senses.title: Unusually special
senses.definition: unusually good, special, or rare, so as to seem unlike anything else
senses.definitionCN: 格外好、特别或罕见，以至于显得不同寻常
senses.example: She has a unique gift for making shy children speak.
senses.exampleCN: 她有一种难得的天赋，能让害羞的孩子开口说话。
senses.why: Marketers and speakers stretch the word from only one to one of a kind in quality.
senses.whyCN: 广告与演讲把这个词从「只有一个」扩展到「品质上独一类」。

senses.title: The one thing itself
senses.definition: a rare noun use for the single object or person that has no match
senses.definitionCN: 少见的名词用法，指没有相配之物的那一个对象或人
senses.example: Collectors speak of the unique, the piece that no museum can pair.
senses.exampleCN: 收藏家会说起「孤品」，那种任何博物馆都配不成对的物件。
senses.why: Adjectives for state are often turned into nouns, and this one names the matchless thing.
senses.whyCN: 表示状态的形容词常转作名词，这个词指那件无从配对之物。

senses.title: As a key in systems
senses.definition: in computing, identifying one record or account and no other
senses.definitionCN: 在计算机领域，指只标识一条记录或一个账户而不标识其他
senses.example: Every account is given a unique number that is never reused.
senses.exampleCN: 每个账户都被分配一个从不重复使用的唯一编号。
senses.why: Machines need the strict sense: one identifier, one record, no exceptions.
senses.whyCN: 机器需要最严格的意义：一个标识对应一条记录，没有例外。

intro.en: Unique comes from a Latin word built on one, and it reached English through French.
intro.cn: unique 来自一个以「一」为核心构成的拉丁语词，经法语进入英语。

items.en: Unus meant one, and the adjective unicus meant single, sole, of one only.
items.cn: 拉丁语 unus 意为「一」，形容词 unicus 意为「唯一的、单独的」。

items.en: French took unicus as un, and formed univ meaning only one, the source of the English word.
items.cn: 法语把 unicus 化约成 un，并构成 univ，义为「只有一个」，是英语词的来源。

items.en: Sixteenth-century French unique was used for the sole example of a thing, with no rival.
items.cn: 十六世纪的法语 unique 用于指某物唯一的实例，没有对手。

items.en: English borrowed the word for things that stand alone in their class, from coins to paintings.
items.cn: 英语借入这个词，指在其类别中单独存在的对象，从钱币到绘画。

items.en: The weaker sense of merely unusual or very good spread in advertising and everyday praise.
items.cn: 「仅仅罕见或很好」这种较弱的意义在广告与日常赞美中扩散开来。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words built on the one root; the near-meaning group gathers adjectives of rarity and distinction at different strengths.
note.cn: 形近组收以「一」这一词根构成的词；近义组收表示稀有与出众的形容词，力度各不相同。

entries.definition: The adverb meaning in a way that belongs to no other.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，义为「独特地、唯一地」。

entries.definition: The noun for the quality of being the only one of its kind.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「独特性、唯一性」。

entries.definition: Speaking or singing at the same pitch together; it shares the one but not the sole.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「齐声、同音」，共享「一」而不含「唯一」。

entries.definition: A single thing or measure treated as one.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「单位、单元」，即被当作一个的整体。

entries.definition: The joining of separate things into one.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「联合、工会」，把分开之物合成一个。

entries.definition: Exceptional or odd; in grammar, one rather than many.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「非凡的、奇特的」，语法中表示单数。

entries.definition: The only one there is, as in the sole owner; narrower and more legal.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「唯一的」，如唯一所有人，范围更窄、更偏法律。

entries.definition: Not often found; it does not claim that only one exists.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「稀少的」，并不主张只有一件。

entries.definition: Easy to tell apart from others; about difference rather than number.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「有特色的」，强调区别而非数量。

entries.definition: Having no equal at all; a stronger, more formal claim than unique.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「无与伦比的」，比 unique 更强、更正式。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the Latin one at the centre of the word and the phrases it really appears in.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些钩子使用这个词核心处的拉丁语「一」，以及它真实出现的搭配。

normal.en: Uni- is one: a unique thing is a class with a single member.
normal.cn: uni- 是「一」：unique 之物就是只有一个成员的那一类。

normal.en: Fingerprints are the textbook example: unique even for twins.
normal.cn: 指纹是教科书式的例子：连双胞胎之间也独一无二。

normal.en: Unique to means found in one place only.
normal.cn: unique to 意为只存在于某一处。

normal.en: The word has no true comparative in strict use: something cannot be more one of a kind.
normal.cn: 严格来说这个词没有真正的比较级：一样东西不能更「独一份」。

normal.en: In computing a unique number may never be reused.
normal.cn: 在计算机里，唯一编号绝不可以重复使用。

abstract.en: Picture a key cut for one lock only: no copy of the blank exists, so the key is its own justification.
abstract.cn: 想象一把只为一把锁配出的钥匙：坯子没有第二份，钥匙本身就说明了一切。

abstract.en: Uniqueness is a relation, not a quality: a thing is unique only when compared with the whole class.
abstract.cn: 独特性是一种关系而非性质：只有与整个类别相比，一样东西才成立为唯一。

abstract.en: Advertising loves the word because it turns rarity into worth.
abstract.cn: 广告喜欢这个词，因为它把稀有变成了价值。

examples.en: This valley has a unique climate, with rain on one side and dry wind on the other.
examples.cn: 这条山谷的气候独一无二，一侧多雨，另一侧却是干风。

examples.en: The custom is unique to the islanders.
examples.cn: 这一习俗为岛上居民所特有。

examples.en: Each ticket carries a unique code for entry.
examples.cn: 每张票都带有一个入场专用的唯一编码。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「优尼克」——优尼这一款只有一件，克数也不重样：独一无二

root: 源自拉丁语 unus「一」所生的 unicus「唯一的、单独的」，经古法语与法语 univ 进入英语；本义是「同类中仅此一件」，近代又扩展出「罕见、极好」的较弱意义。

sensesIntro.en: Five senses of unique all turn on the number one: one member of a class, one place of origin, one of a kind in quality, the matchless object itself, or one key in a system.
sensesIntro.cn: unique 的五个义项都围绕「一」：类别里只有一员、只出现在一处、品质上独一类、那件无从配对之物本身，或系统中唯一的一把钥匙。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a single vessel fired once, with no mould left and no second copy.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只只烧过一次的瓷器，模具没有留下，也没有第二件。

branches.en: THE CLASS: the word marks a class with only one member.
branches.cn: 类别线：这个词标记一个只有一名成员的类别。

branches.en: THE PLACE: the one location or group that has it.
branches.cn: 地点线：拥有它的那唯一一处地方或人群。

branches.en: THE PRAISE: rarity turns into praise of quality.
branches.cn: 赞美线：稀有转为对品质的赞美。

branches.en: THE OBJECT: the matchless thing can be named as a noun.
branches.cn: 物件线：那件无从配对之物可用名词来命名。

branches.en: THE SYSTEM: machines need one number for one record.
branches.cn: 系统线：机器需要一号对一记录。

intro.en: Unique is almost all root: a Latin word for one, plus a small adjective ending and English suffixes.
intro.cn: unique 几乎全是词根：一个拉丁语「一」词，加一个小小的形容词词尾与英语后缀。

latinIntro.en: Unus and unicus are both recorded Latin words, so nothing in the core is reconstructed.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 unus 与 unicus 均有文献记录，核心部分不需要重构。

items.exampleCN: 这个前缀是这个词的核心。

definition_zh: 基础；底部；基地；以……为基础
definition_en: the bottom part, a main place or centre, or to use something as a starting point
core_image: 石柱最下端一块宽厚的基石
scene: 山脚下搭起一片帐篷。 The camp was built at the base of the mountain.
sceneCN: 这里 base 是「底部」（第 2 个义项：物体最下面的部分）；句意是营地建在山脚。

derivatives.zh: 由 base 加 -ic 构成，义为「基本的」
同源词，来自希腊语 basis，义为「基础；依据」
由 base 加 -d 构成，义为「以……为基础的」

senses.title: A foundation
senses.definition: the main idea or support that something rests on
senses.definitionCN: 某事物所依靠的主要思想或支撑
senses.example: The argument has a weak base.
senses.exampleCN: 这个论点的基础很薄弱。
senses.why: Base came from Greek basis, a step or pedestal, so it first names what holds something up.
senses.whyCN: base 来自希腊语 basis「台阶、基座」，所以它首先指支撑某物的东西。

senses.title: The bottom part
senses.definition: the lowest part of an object
senses.definitionCN: 物体最下面的部分
senses.example: The camp was built at the base of the mountain.
senses.exampleCN: 营地建在山脚。
senses.why: The pedestal is the bottom of a column, so the word names the lowest part of anything.
senses.whyCN: 基座是柱子最下面的部分，所以这个词指任何物体的底部。

senses.title: A main centre
senses.definition: a main place from which work or travel starts
senses.definitionCN: 工作或出行所依托的主要地点
senses.example: The team returned to its base before dark.
senses.exampleCN: 队伍在天黑前返回基地。
senses.why: A place you start from and return to works like a base under a structure, which produced this sense.
senses.whyCN: 出发并返回的地点像建筑下的基座，于是产生「基地」义。

definition_en: to win against an opponent, or to make a plan fail; also a loss in a contest
core_image: 对手低下头，慢慢走出场地
scene: 终场哨响，主队球员垂着头走向更衣室，看台上没有一个人说话。 The young team defeated the champions by one goal.
sceneCN: 这里 defeat 指「击败」（第 1 个义项：在比赛或争斗中战胜对手）；句意是这支年轻队伍以一球之差战胜了冠军队。

senses.title: Win a contest against someone
senses.definition: to win a victory over an opponent in a game, battle or election
senses.definitionCN: 在比赛、战斗或选举中战胜对手
senses.example: Our team defeated the visitors by two goals.
senses.exampleCN: 我们队以两球战胜了客队。
senses.why: A contest ends the moment one side can no longer answer.
senses.whyCN: 比赛在一方再也还不了手的那一刻就结束了。

senses.title: Make a hope or plan fail
senses.definition: to cause a plan, hope or purpose to come to nothing
senses.definitionCN: 使计划、希望或目的无法实现
senses.example: The heavy rain defeated our plan for a picnic.
senses.exampleCN: 大雨让我们的野餐计划落空了。
senses.why: A plan can be beaten just as a person can be beaten.
senses.whyCN: 计划也会像人一样被打败。

senses.title: A loss in a contest
senses.definition: the fact of losing a game, battle or election
senses.definitionCN: 在比赛、战斗或选举中输掉的事实
senses.example: The defeat left the players silent in the changing room.
senses.exampleCN: 这场失败让球员们在更衣室里一言不发。
senses.why: Every victory leaves behind a second word for the other side.
senses.whyCN: 每一场胜利，都会给另一方留下另一个词。

intro.en: Defeat came to English through French, but its pieces are Latin: dis- meaning apart and facere meaning to do.
intro.cn: defeat 经法语进入英语，但零件是拉丁的：dis- 表示分开，facere 表示做。

items.en: Disfacere meant to undo or destroy what had been made.
items.cn: disfacere 意为把做好的东西拆掉、毁掉。

items.en: Desfait named the state of being undone.
items.cn: desfait 指被拆散、被毁掉的状态。

items.en: English took the word as a noun for a lost battle.
items.cn: 英语把它借来，作名词指一场打输的仗。

items.en: The verb grew beside the noun and took over the action.
items.cn: 动词在旁边长出来，接过「打败」这个动作。

items.en: A team can defeat a rival, and a problem can defeat a plan.
items.cn: 如今队伍能击败对手，难题也能让计划落空。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the de- opening, and the meaning group moves from beating someone to mastering a difficulty.
note.cn: 形近组都以 de- 开头，近义组则从打赢对手一路走到克服困难。

normalIntro.en: These hooks start with the whistle at the end of a match and end with a plan that never happened.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子从比赛结束的哨声开始，落到一个没能实现的计划。

normal.en: The scoreboard is honest: it says who answered last.
normal.cn: 记分牌最诚实，它只写谁最后还了手。

normal.en: A team can be beaten, and so can a good idea.
normal.cn: 队伍会被打败，好主意也一样。

normal.en: Rain does not argue with a picnic; it simply defeats it.

normal.en: In defeat a crowd learns the sound of its own silence.
normal.cn: 在失败里，人群听见了自己沉默的声音。

normal.en: Defeat and defend are twins: one takes the field, one guards it.
normal.cn: defeat 和 defend 像双胞胎：一个上场攻，一个守家门。

abstract.en: Picture a flag folded and carried off the field.
abstract.cn: 想象一面旗被叠好，带离场地。

abstract.en: Picture a picnic basket still packed while rain hits the window.
abstract.cn: 想象雨打着窗，野餐篮还原封未动。

abstract.en: Picture a head lowered just enough to be seen.
abstract.cn: 想象一个头低下去，刚好让人看见。

examples.en: After the defeat, the coach spoke to each player alone.

root: 来自拉丁语 disfacere，由 dis-（分开）与 facere（做）组成，本义是把做好的东西拆掉、毁掉；经古法语 desfait 进入英语。它先指打输一场仗的结果，十六世纪起动词用法兴盛，后来又引申为让计划、希望落空。

sensesIntro.en: From a rival who cannot answer, to a plan that cannot happen, to the word for losing.

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one side walks off the field with a lowered head.
core.cn: 核心意象：一方低着头走出场地。

branches.en: The first sense is a rival who can no longer answer.
branches.cn: 第一个义项是再也还不了手的对手。

branches.en: The same force applied to a plan leaves it undone.
branches.cn: 同样的力量落到计划上，计划就做不成了。

branches.en: Seen from the other side, the same event is called a loss.

branches.en: Both senses describe something that stopped before it finished.

intro.en: Defeat grows a small family of nouns about giving up and adjectives about never being beaten.
intro.cn: defeat 长出一小族词：有表示放弃的名词，也有表示不曾被击败的形容词。

senses.title: Health, happiness, and comfort

senses.example: Parents put the welfare of their children first.
senses.exampleCN: 父母把孩子的幸福安康放在第一位。
senses.why: The old wish of a good journey broadened into a general state of faring well.
senses.whyCN: 古时「一路安好」的祝愿，扩展为「过得好」的总体状态。

senses.title: Care for the well-being of others
senses.definition: attention to making sure someone is safe, healthy, and all right
senses.definitionCN: 确保他人安全、健康无恙的关心与照管
senses.example: The teacher reported her concern for the child's welfare.
senses.exampleCN: 老师表达了对那个孩子福祉的担忧。
senses.why: If faring well is a state, looking after it becomes a duty of care.
senses.whyCN: 「过得好」是一种状态，守护这种状态便成为照管之责。

senses.title: Organization for animal or child welfare
senses.definition: organized efforts to protect animals, children, or other vulnerable groups
senses.definitionCN: 保护动物、儿童等弱势群体的有组织行动
senses.example: She volunteers at an animal welfare society.
senses.exampleCN: 她在一家动物保护协会做志愿者。
senses.why: Care for the weak becomes an institution with its own name and flag.
senses.whyCN: 对弱者的照管结成机构，拥有自己的名义与旗帜。

senses.title: State aid to people in need
senses.definition: money and services given by the government to people who are poor, ill, or unemployed
senses.definitionCN: 政府向贫困、患病或失业者提供的金钱与服务
senses.example: After losing his job, he lived on welfare for two years.
senses.exampleCN: 失业后，他靠救济金生活了两年。
senses.why: When the state takes over the old duty of care, its payments inherit the word welfare.
senses.whyCN: 当国家接过旧的照管之责，它的补助金便沿用了 welfare 这个词。

senses.title: The welfare system itself
senses.definition: the whole set of public programs that support citizens' basic needs
senses.definitionCN: 保障公民基本需求的整套公共制度
senses.example: Debates about reforming the welfare system never end.
senses.exampleCN: 关于改革福利制度的争论从未停止。
senses.why: Individual aid adds up to a system, and the system takes the name of its purpose.
senses.whyCN: 一项项补助汇成制度，制度便以其目的命名。

senses.title: Personal benefit or interest
senses.definition: what is best for a person's interests, as in decisions made for someone's welfare
senses.definitionCN: 就某人利益而言的最佳安排
senses.example: The court decides custody based on the child's welfare.
senses.exampleCN: 法庭根据孩子的利益来裁决抚养权。
senses.why: Faring well narrows again to whatever arrangement serves one person best.
senses.whyCN: 「过得好」又收窄为对某个人最有利的安排。

senses.title: Welfare as collective prosperity
senses.definition: the shared well-being of a whole society or nation
senses.definitionCN: 整个社会或国家共享的安康
senses.example: Economic growth should serve the welfare of all citizens.
senses.exampleCN: 经济增长应服务于全体公民的福祉。
senses.why: The same good state is measured over a whole people, becoming a goal of politics.
senses.whyCN: 同样的好状态被放大到整个民族头上，成为政治的目标。

senses.title: Welfare officer or worker
senses.definition: used in job titles for those who look after others' well-being
senses.definitionCN: 用于照顾他人福祉的岗位名称
senses.example: The school appointed a student welfare officer.
senses.exampleCN: 学校任命了一名学生福利干事。
senses.why: Institutions attach the word to the person who performs the care.
senses.whyCN: 机构把这个词安到执行照管的那个人头上。

intro.en: Welfare is a native compound of well and fare, literally faring well, with no Latin or French borrowing involved.
intro.cn: welfare 是 well 与 fare 的本土复合词，字面即「过得好」，不含拉丁或法语借词。

items.en: *wel- meant well or wish, and *faran meant to travel or go on a journey.
items.cn: 日耳曼语 *wel- 意为「好、愿」，*faran 意为「出行、行进」。

items.en: Wel and faran existed separately; the compound wel faran meant to fare well, to get along fine.
items.cn: 古英语 wel 与 faran 各自独立；组合 wel faran 意为「过得好、顺遂」。

items.en: The compound welfare is attested from about the fourteenth century, still meaning good fortune or happiness.
items.cn: 复合词 welfare 约于十四世纪见诸文献，仍指好运或幸福。

items.en: Welfare expanded to organized care, founding welfare societies and welfare work.
items.cn: 十八至十九世纪，welfare 扩展到有组织的关怀，出现福利社团与福利工作。

items.en: The modern sense of government aid crystallized with the welfare state after the Second World War.
items.cn: 二战后随「福利国家」兴起，政府救济的现代义定型。

items.en: Welfare now spans personal happiness, public aid, and animal protection alike.
items.cn: 如今 welfare 兼指个人幸福、公共救助与动物保护。

note.en: Welfare shares its two native parts with well-being, farewell, and welcome, and is often swapped loosely with benefit.
note.cn: welfare 的两个本土成分也出现在 well-being、farewell、welcome 中，日常又常与 benefit 混用。

entries.definition: the state of being comfortable and healthy

entries.definition: to greet someone with pleasure
entries.definitionCN: 欢迎。同为 wel-（安好）词族

entries.definition: a good state of health and mind
entries.definitionCN: 安康。侧重身心状态，welfare 更偏制度与救助

entries.definition: money or advantage given or gained
entries.definitionCN: 救济金；好处。具体到钱物，welfare 更宏观

entries.definition: help given to those in need

normalIntro.cn: welfare 自己就讲清了自己：well + fare，过得好。

normal.en: well + fare: to go through life doing well.

normal.en: farewell is the same words reversed: good journey out.

abstract.cn: 看社区中心里排队领取补助表格的人们。

examples.en: The charity works for the welfare of homeless children.
examples.cn: 这家慈善机构为无家可归儿童的福祉而工作。

examples.en: Unemployment welfare kept the family going that winter.
examples.cn: 那年冬天，失业救济金撑起了这个家。

examples.en: Laws on animal welfare have grown stricter.
examples.cn: 动物福利方面的法律日趋严格。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「维尔费」——维尔一家生活遇困难，政府「费」心补贴，这就是「福利」。用「国家费心保障」绑定救济义。

root: welfare 为古英语本土复合词，由 wel（好、安好，well 的古老形式）+ faran（出行、过日子）构成，本义「过得好、顺遂」。同族词 farewell（fare + well，「一路安好」，用作送别语）。十四世纪定型为名词，二十世纪随福利国家制度获得「政府救济」义。

sensesIntro.en: From faring well on a journey, welfare grows into personal happiness, duty of care, protection societies, state aid, the whole system, individual best interest, collective prosperity, and care job titles.
sensesIntro.cn: 从旅途顺遂出发，welfare 长出个人幸福、照管之责、保护事业、国家救济、整套制度、个人最佳利益、公共福祉与照管岗位名义。

branches.en: looking after that state becomes a duty and a job
branches.cn: 守护这种状态成为职责与岗位

branches.en: the duty is organized to protect the vulnerable
branches.cn: 照管之责组织起来，保护弱者

intro.en: Welfare is a compound of two native words, and its family shows how wel- and fare combine in English.
intro.cn: welfare 由两个本土词复合而成，其词族展示 wel- 与 fare 在英语中的组合方式。

latinIntro.en: As a Germanic compound, welfare has no Latin relatives; the Latin entries stay empty.
latinIntro.cn: 作为日耳曼复合词，welfare 没有拉丁同源词，拉丁条目留空。

definition_zh: 仅仅；完全；纯粹地；纯洁地
definition_en: only, completely, and for no other reason or purpose than the one that is stated
core_image: 一张空桌上只放着一支笔，别的什么都没有
scene: 排练结束后，有人问那位老人为什么每周都来帮忙，他摆摆手，说自己只是喜欢听孩子们唱歌。 He came purely out of curiosity, with no plan to buy anything.
sceneCN: 这里取「仅仅、完全」（第 1 个义项：所说原因是唯一涉及的原因）；句意是他来纯粹出于好奇，并没有买东西的打算。老人摆手不收报酬的动作就是线索。

pos.zh: 仅仅；完全；纯粹地；纯洁地

derivatives.zh: purely 的词基，去掉副词词尾 -ly 即得，义为「纯的；纯粹的」
由 pure 加名词后缀 -ity 构成，义为「纯净；纯度」
由拉丁词干 pur- 加 -ify 构成，义为「净化；提纯」

senses.title: Only, and nothing else
senses.definition: used to show that the reason or quality just named is the only one involved
senses.definitionCN: 用来表明刚才所说的原因或性质是唯一涉及的
senses.example: The meeting was called purely to explain the new rules.
senses.exampleCN: 召开这次会议只是为了解释新规定。
senses.why: The -ly ending turns the adjective into a lens: whatever follows is seen as nothing but itself, with every other motive removed.
senses.whyCN: -ly 把形容词变成一面透镜：后面跟的东西只被看成它本身，其他动机全被剔除。

senses.title: For no other purpose than the one named
senses.definition: done only for the reason given, with no hidden or practical aim
senses.definitionCN: 只因为所说的理由而做，没有隐藏的或实际的目的
senses.example: She joined the choir purely for the pleasure of singing.
senses.exampleCN: 她加入合唱团纯粹是为了唱歌的乐趣。
senses.why: This is the first sense applied to a motive: when one purpose is named alone, the word quietly denies that money, fame or duty played any part.
senses.whyCN: 这是第一个义项用在动机上：当只点出一个目的时，这个词就在悄悄否认金钱、名声或义务起过作用。

senses.title: In theory rather than in practice
senses.definition: considered as an idea or a model, without being tested in real conditions
senses.definitionCN: 作为观念或模型来考虑，未在真实条件下检验
senses.example: Purely theoretically, the bridge could hold twice that weight.
senses.exampleCN: 纯从理论上说，那座桥能承受两倍的重量。
senses.why: A pure substance has nothing foreign in it, and a purely theoretical question has no case, no data and no site mixed into it.
senses.whyCN: 纯物质里没有外来成分，纯理论问题里也不掺具体案例、数据和现场，两者的结构是一样的。

senses.title: In a clean or blameless way
senses.definition: in a manner free from wrongdoing, used mostly of living or behaving
senses.definitionCN: 以没有过失的方式，多用于形容生活或行为
senses.example: He lived purely and gave away most of what he earned.
senses.exampleCN: 他生活清白，把挣来的大部分都捐了出去。
senses.why: The moral branch of pure reaches the adverb here: to act purely is to act with nothing soiled in the intention.
senses.whyCN: pure 的道德分支在这里落到副词上：purely 地做事，就是意图里没有任何被弄脏的部分。

intro.en: Purely is the English adverb built on pure, which came from Latin purus through Old French; its ending is the native English -ly.
intro.cn: purely 是由 pure 构成的英语副词，而 pure 经古法语来自拉丁语 purus；它的词尾是英语本土的 -ly。

items.en: Purus meant clean and unmixed, and it is the source of the whole English family.
items.cn: purus 意为干净、不混杂，是英语这一族词的源头。

items.en: Old French kept pur for clean and unmixed and also for what is morally blameless, and English borrowed the adjective from it.
items.cn: 古法语用 pur 表示干净、不混杂，也指道德上没有过失的；英语从这个形容词借入。

items.en: Middle English pure named what is free of mixture, and the adverb was then built on it inside English.
items.cn: 中古英语的 pure 指没有混杂的东西，副词随后在英语内部由它构成。

items.en: The adverbial ending came from Old English -lice, which became -ly and turns an adjective into a word about manner.
items.cn: 副词词尾来自古英语 -lice，后来写作 -ly，把形容词变成描述方式的一类词。

items.en: Modern English uses purely mostly as a limiter, telling the listener that nothing else stands behind what was said.
items.cn: 现代英语中的 purely 多半起限定作用，告诉听者所说的事情背后没有别的东西。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the adjective that stands behind the adverb and its closest relatives; the near-meaning group gathers other adverbs of limitation.
note.cn: 形近组收这个副词背后的形容词及其最近的同族词；近义组收其他表示限定的副词。

entries.definition: The adjective from which this adverb is built.
entries.definitionCN: 构成这个副词的原形容词。

entries.definition: The quality of being pure.
To make something clean by removing what is unwanted.
entries.definitionCN: 除去不需要的成分使某物变干净。

entries.definition: A person who keeps strictly to the original standards of a subject.
entries.definitionCN: 严格坚持某领域原有标准的人。

entries.definition: Only, and nothing more.
For one reason only, or in a plain way.
For that one reason and no other.

normalIntro.en: The word is the adjective for clean lifted into an adverb of narrowing, and its memories sit on the -ly ending and on the idea of one cause only.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词是把表示「干净」的形容词抬升为起收窄作用的副词，记忆点落在 -ly 词尾和「只有一个原因」上。

normal.en: Purely is pure plus -ly, so it does to the adjective what quickly does to quick.
normal.cn: purely 是 pure 加 -ly，它对形容词做的事，和 quickly 对 quick 做的一样。

normal.en: The -ly ending came from Old English -lice and has always answered the question of how.
normal.cn: -ly 词尾来自古英语 -lice，一直用来回答「怎样」这个问题。

normal.en: Purely by chance removes human intention from the sentence, leaving only chance in the frame.
normal.cn: purely by chance 把人的意图从句子中拿掉，画面里只剩「偶然」。

normal.en: Purely theoretical is the adverb version of pure science: the practical part has been filtered out.
normal.cn: purely theoretical 是 pure science 的副词版：实用的部分已经被滤掉。

normal.en: The moral use, as in living purely, is the oldest layer of purus still visible in an everyday adverb.
normal.cn: 表示道德义的 living purely，是 purus 最古老的一层仍留在日常副词里的痕迹。

abstract.en: An adverb of purity works like a spotlight: it darkens everything except the one thing named.
abstract.cn: 表示纯粹的副词像一盏聚光灯：除了被点到的那样东西，其余全被压暗。

abstract.en: Saying purely is a way of closing doors, one by one, until only one reason is left in the room.
abstract.cn: 说 purely 就是把门一扇扇关上，直到屋里只剩一个理由。

abstract.en: The word is small but it carries a whole claim about cause, which is why it so often ends an argument.
abstract.cn: 这个词很小，却包含了一整套关于因果的主张，所以它常常能给争论画上句号。

examples.en: The meeting was called purely to explain the new rules.
examples.cn: 召开这次会议只是为了解释新规定。

examples.en: She joined the choir purely for the pleasure of singing.
examples.cn: 她加入合唱团纯粹是为了唱歌的乐趣。

examples.en: He came purely out of curiosity, with no plan to buy anything.
examples.cn: 他来纯粹出于好奇，并没有买东西的打算。

dict_mnemonic.text: 读音近「漂离」——把别的东西都漂洗掉，只剩下本身，就是纯粹地。

root: 拉丁语 purus（干净、不混杂）经古法语 pur 进入英语作 pure，再加古英语副词词尾 -lice（今 -ly）构成 purely。

sensesIntro.en: The core is one thing with nothing behind it; the senses divide into a single reason, a single purpose, theory without practice, and a blameless life.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是「只有这一样，背后别无他物」；义项分成唯一的原因、唯一的目的、脱离实践的理论，以及没有过失的生活。

core.cn: 核心意象：一张空桌上只放着一支笔。

branches.en: a single pen left on an otherwise empty desk
branches.cn: 空桌上只留一支笔

branches.en: a man waving away payment for his help
branches.cn: 老人摆手不收报酬

branches.en: a calculation done on paper and never built
branches.cn: 只在纸上算过、从未建造

branches.en: a life with nothing hidden in it
branches.cn: 没有隐藏之事的一生

branches.en: a word that narrows a sentence down to one cause
branches.cn: 把整句话收窄到唯一原因的一个词

intro.en: A Latin adjective for clean and a native English adverb ending hold the word together, and the same stem also grows nouns and a verb.
intro.cn: 表示「干净」的拉丁语形容词与英语本土副词词尾共同支撑这个词，同一词干还长出名词与动词。

latinIntro.en: Latin purus, clean and unmixed, and the noun puritas stand behind the adjective, and English added the adverbial ending -ly to form this word.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 purus（干净、不混杂）与名词 puritas 是那个形容词的来源，英语再加副词词尾 -ly 构成了这个词。

items.meaning: one who insists on pure standards

definition_en: a strong feeling of excitement and interest in something
core_image: 胸口像被一团火点着，忍不住向前倾身去做那件事
scene: 听说球队要打决赛，整条街的人都兴奋地讨论起来。 When the team reached the final, the whole street discussed it with enthusiasm.
sceneCN: 这里 enthusiasm 是「热情」（第 1 个义项：强烈的兴奋与兴趣）；句意：球队打进决赛时，整条街的人都热情地讨论这件事。

senses.title: Strong excitement and interest
senses.definition: a strong feeling of eagerness and interest in something
senses.definitionCN: 对某事物强烈的渴望与兴趣
senses.example: She spoke about the project with great enthusiasm.
senses.exampleCN: 她满腔热情地谈起这个项目。
senses.why: The Greek source describes a god within, and that inner fire becomes strong excited interest.
senses.whyCN: 希腊语来源描述「心中有神」，这种内心之火就变成强烈的兴奋与兴趣。

senses.title: An object of passionate interest
senses.definition: an activity or subject that someone pursues with great eagerness
senses.definitionCN: 某人满怀热忱去从事的活动或主题
senses.example: Gardening is one of her lifelong enthusiasms.
senses.exampleCN: 园艺是她终身的爱好之一。
senses.why: The feeling is transferred to the thing that produces it.
senses.whyCN: 这种情感被转移到产生它的事物上。

senses.title: Fervent devotion to a cause
senses.definition: intense and sometimes uncritical devotion to a belief or cause
senses.definitionCN: 对信念或事业强烈、有时缺乏批判的投入
senses.example: His early enthusiasm for the movement later cooled.
senses.exampleCN: 他早年对这场运动的狂热后来冷却了。
senses.why: The original religious intensity survives in this formal sense of devoted zeal.
senses.whyCN: 原初的宗教强度保留在这个正式的「热诚」义项中。

intro.en: Enthusiasm comes from Greek enthousiasmos, divine possession, from entheos, having a god within, built on en- and theos, god.
intro.cn: enthusiasm 来自希腊语 enthousiasmos（神灵附体），源于 entheos（心中有神），由 en- 与 theos（神）构成。

items.en: Theos means god.
items.cn: theos 意为神。

items.en: Entheos means having a god within, inspired.
items.cn: entheos 意为心中有神、受神灵启发的。

items.en: Enthousiasmos means divine possession or inspired frenzy.
items.cn: enthousiasmos 意为神灵附体、受神启的狂热。

items.en: Enthusiasmus carries the term into learned Latin.
items.cn: enthusiasmus 把这个词带入学术拉丁语。

items.en: English adopts enthusiasm for possession by a god.
items.cn: 到 16 世纪，英语用 enthusiasm 表示神灵附体。

items.en: The word now means strong excited interest in almost anything.
items.cn: 现代英语中，这个词表示对几乎任何事物的强烈兴趣。

note.en: Enthusiasm is a fire word, and it sits near its own family and near words for passion and zeal.
note.cn: enthusiasm 是一个「火焰」词，与自身词族以及表示激情和热忱的词相邻。

entries.definition: a person who is very interested in something
showing strong excitement
in an eager and excited way
a very strong feeling or interest
great energy for a cause
the state of wanting something very much

normalIntro.en: Enthusiasm comes from Greek entheos, having a god within: the word pictures fire inside a person.
normalIntro.cn: enthusiasm 来自希腊语 entheos（心中有神）：这个词描绘人体内的一团火。

normal.en: Theos means god, so enthusiasm once meant divine possession.
normal.cn: theos 意为神，所以 enthusiasm 原指神灵附体。

normal.en: Modern enthusiasm is simply strong excitement and interest.
normal.cn: 现代的 enthusiasm 就是强烈的兴奋与兴趣。

normal.en: Enthusiasm for something is the usual pattern with a noun.
normal.cn: enthusiasm for something 是常见的名词搭配。

normal.en: The adjective is enthusiastic, and the person is an enthusiast.
normal.cn: 形容词是 enthusiastic，指人是 enthusiast。

normal.en: Compare passion: passion burns quietly, while enthusiasm shows itself openly.
normal.cn: 对比 passion：passion 安静地燃烧，enthusiasm 则外露。

abstract.en: Picture a spark catching dry grass and spreading fast.
abstract.cn: 想象火星落在干草上，迅速蔓延。

abstract.en: Imagine a child pulling a parent toward a festival tent.
abstract.cn: 想象孩子拉着父母往节日的帐篷跑。

abstract.en: Think of a room leaning forward to hear one voice.
abstract.cn: 想象整个房间的人都前倾身体听一个声音。

examples.en: She spoke about the project with great enthusiasm.
examples.cn: 她满腔热情地谈起这个项目。

examples.en: His enthusiasm for music began at school.
examples.cn: 他对音乐的热情始于学校。

examples.en: The crowd's enthusiasm lifted the players.
examples.cn: 观众的热情鼓舞了球员。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「en-theos」——心里住着一位神，所以热情高涨；这只是词源拆解式联想，与日常读音无关。

root: 希腊语 theos（神）→ entheos（心中有神的）→ enthousiasmos（神灵附体般的激情）→ 拉丁语 enthusiasmus → 英语 enthusiasm。

sensesIntro.en: The word begins as divine possession, softens into religious fervor, and finally becomes the everyday fire of strong interest.
sensesIntro.cn: 这个词最初指神灵附体，后淡化为宗教热诚，最终成为日常所说的强烈兴趣之火。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a fire lit inside a person that pushes them forward.
core.cn: 核心意象：心中燃起一团火，推着人向前。

branches.en: Strong excited interest is the everyday modern sense.
branches.cn: 强烈兴奋的兴趣，是现代日常义项。

branches.en: The thing that lights the fire becomes an enthusiasm too.
branches.cn: 点燃火焰的事物本身也被称作 enthusiasm。

branches.en: Devotion to a cause keeps the original intensity.
branches.cn: 对事业的投入保留了原初的强度。

branches.en: People feel enthusiasm, and their hobbies are their enthusiasms.
branches.cn: 人怀有热情，而爱好就是他们所热衷的事物。

branches.en: A lifelong hobby and a cause can both command devotion.
branches.cn: 终身爱好与事业都能赢得投入。

intro.en: Enthusiasm is a Greek word that reached English through Latin, and English endings form its modern family.
intro.cn: enthusiasm 是经拉丁语进入英语的希腊词，现代词族由英语词尾构成。

latinIntro.en: Greek theos means god, and entheos means having a god within; Latin enthusiasmus carries the word westward.
latinIntro.cn: 希腊语 theos 表示神，entheos 表示心中有神；拉丁语 enthusiasmus 把这个词带向西方。

items.exampleCN: en- 出现在 entheos 开头。

items.example: Theos is the heart of the word.
Entheos gives the image of inner fire.
items.exampleCN: entheos 提供内心之火的画面。

items.example: Enthousiasmos is the direct Greek source.
items.exampleCN: enthousiasmos 是直接的希腊语来源。

items.example: Enthusiasmus carries the term into Latin.
items.exampleCN: enthusiasmus 把这个词带入拉丁语。

items.example: Enthusiasm is the modern English form.

items.meaningCN: 表示状态或做法的词尾
items.example: The noun keeps the Greek -ismos shape.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词保留希腊语 -ismos 的形态。

items.example: Enthusiastic adds -ic to the noun stem.

definition_zh: 原木；圆木；航海日志；记录簿；记录；累计达到（里程、工时）
definition_en: a thick piece of cut or fallen tree; an official written record of events on a ship or aircraft; to write down events or figures in such a record; to travel or work a stated amount that is added to a total
core_image: 斧头落下去，树干断成一截一截，木纹里还渗着树脂
scene: 码头边的空地上，卡车后挡板放下，几截树干滚了下来。 A thick log rolled off the truck and landed in the mud.
sceneCN: 这里是「伐下的整段树干」（第 1 个义项：未经加工的原木）；句意为一段粗大的原木从卡车上滚下来，落进了泥地里。

pos.zh: 记录；把……记入日志；累计达到

derivatives.zh: 由 log 加表示「人」的后缀 -er 构成，义为「伐木工；记录员」
由 log 加 -ing 构成，义为「伐木作业」
由 log 与 book 复合而成，义为「日志簿；记录本」
由 back 与 log 复合而成，义为「积压未办的工作」
由 log 与 in 复合而成，义为「登录」

senses.title: A thick piece of cut tree
senses.definition: a thick piece of wood cut from a tree, or a whole trunk lying where it fell
senses.definitionCN: 从树上砍下的粗大木段，或倒在地上未经处理的整根树干
senses.example: The cabin walls were built from rough logs.
senses.exampleCN: 小木屋的墙是用粗糙的原木垒起来的。
senses.why: Middle English logge already meant a lump of wood, and this concrete sense has stayed at the centre of the word ever since.
senses.whyCN: 中古英语 logge 已经指一截木头，这个最具体的义项从中古一直留到今天，是整组词义的中心。

senses.title: An official record of a voyage or flight
senses.definition: an official written record of events kept on a ship, an aircraft or a machine
senses.definitionCN: 船、飞机或机器上保存的正式事件记录
senses.example: The captain wrote the storm into the ship's log.
senses.exampleCN: 船长把这场风暴写进了航海日志。
senses.why: Sailors measured speed by throwing a weighted piece of wood overboard and reading the line; the figures went into a book, and the book took the name of the wood.
senses.whyCN: 船员把一块系着重物的木头抛进海里测速，再读线上的刻度；数字记进本子，本子便沿用了那块木头的名字。

senses.title: To write something down in a record
senses.definition: to write an event, figure or message into an official record as it happens
senses.definitionCN: 把发生的事情、数字或消息在发生时写入正式记录
senses.example: Officers logged every radio message during the night.
senses.exampleCN: 夜里，值班人员把每一条无线电消息都记了下来。
senses.why: Once log named the book, the same word could name the act of writing in it, so the record and the recording share one form.
senses.whyCN: 当 log 指那本簿子之后，同一个词自然也能指在簿子上书写这件事，于是「记录」和「被记录的内容」共用一个形式。

senses.title: To add up distance or working time
senses.definition: to travel or work an amount that is added to a running total
senses.definitionCN: 走过的距离或工作的时间被累加进一个总数
senses.example: The old bus has logged more than a million kilometres.
senses.exampleCN: 这辆旧巴士累计跑了一百多万公里。
senses.why: A logbook keeps a running total, so the verb came to mean reaching a figure that the book will hold.
senses.whyCN: 日志簿记的是一路累加的总数，所以动词又指达到某个会被写进簿子的数字。

intro.en: Log appears in Middle English as a word for a block of wood, and its further origin is uncertain; the record sense grew out of sailors measuring speed with a wooden chip.
intro.cn: log 在中古英语里就指一截木头，更早的来源不确定；记录义则从船员用木块测速这件事上长出来。

items.en: The word is first recorded in Middle English as logge, a block of wood, and no earlier form is securely attested.
items.cn: 这个词最早见于中古英语，写作 logge，指一截木头；更早的形式没有可靠的书面证据。

items.en: Logge named a cut block or a fallen trunk, the rough timber used for walls and for firewood.
items.cn: logge 指砍下的木块或倒下的树干，就是用来垒墙和烧火的粗木料。

items.en: Some dictionaries suggest a connection with Scandinavian words for something lying down, but the link is not certain.
items.cn: 一些词典认为它与斯堪的纳维亚语中表示「躺倒之物」的词有关，但这一联系并不确定。

items.en: A weighted wooden chip was thrown overboard to measure a ship's speed, and the readings were kept in a log book.
items.cn: 人们把一块加重的小木板抛到船外测速，读数记在航海日志里。

items.en: The word extends to any systematic record, then to computer sign-ins and to totals of distance or hours.
items.cn: 词义扩展到任何系统化的记录，再进入计算机登录，也表示里程或工时的累计。

note.en: The look-alike group is built from log plus common English elements; the near-meaning group gathers words for wood and for written records.
note.cn: 形近组由 log 与常见英语成分组合而成；近义组收表示木材和书面记录的词。

entries.definition: An official book in which events are recorded.
entries.definitionCN: 记录事件的正式簿子；日志簿。

entries.definition: A person who cuts timber or keeps a record.
entries.definitionCN: 伐木的人，或负责记录的人。

entries.definition: The business of cutting trees for timber.
entries.definitionCN: 砍树取木材的行业；伐木。

entries.definition: Work that has piled up and is still waiting.
entries.definitionCN: 堆积起来尚未处理的工作；积压。

entries.definition: The act of signing into a computer system.
entries.definitionCN: 登录计算机系统的动作；登录。

entries.definition: Wood prepared for building, or standing trees.
entries.definitionCN: 备好的建筑木材，或尚未砍伐的树木。

entries.definition: A book in which a person writes about each day.
entries.definitionCN: 逐日写下经历的簿子；日记。

entries.definition: A serious record of events or a periodical about them.
entries.definitionCN: 对事件的正式记录，或刊载这类内容的期刊。

entries.definition: A written account of facts kept for the future.
entries.definitionCN: 为日后查阅而留下的事实记载。

normalIntro.en: Log starts as a plain word for a block of wood; the written record comes from the wooden chip sailors threw into the sea.
normalIntro.cn: log 起初只是「一截木头」的朴素说法；书面记录义则来自船员抛进海里的那块木片。

normal.en: Middle English wrote logge for a cut block of wood, and that solid sense never left the word.
normal.cn: 中古英语把砍下的一截木头写作 logge，这个实在的意思一直没有离开这个词。

normal.en: Sailors threw a weighted chip into the water, read the line, and wrote the figures in a book, so the book was named after the wood.
normal.cn: 船员把加重的小木片抛进水里，读线上的刻度，再把数字写进本子，本子便跟着木头得了名。

normal.en: Logger adds -er to log: the person who cuts the timber or keeps the record.
normal.cn: logger 在 log 后加 -er：砍木头的人，或负责记记录的人。

normal.en: Logbook is log and book joined directly, a book that holds the entries.
normal.cn: logbook 是 log 与 book 直接拼在一起，指收纳这些记录的本子。

normal.en: Backlog is back plus log: entries that piled up behind the rest, now any unfinished work.
normal.cn: backlog 是 back 加 log：堆在后面的记录，如今指任何积压未办的工作。

abstract.en: A cut block and a record book share one word, which suggests English treats a countable thing and a checkable trace as close neighbours.
abstract.cn: 一截木头和一本记录簿共用一个词，说明英语把「可数的东西」和「可查的痕迹」看得很近。

abstract.en: The chip thrown overboard is a reminder that a record is built from readings someone can check, not from memory.
abstract.cn: 抛到船外的那块木片提醒人：记录靠的是一次次可以核对的读数，而不是记忆。

abstract.en: Turn the pages of a log and time is cut into lines, which is the most practical picture this word offers.
abstract.cn: 一页页翻日志，时间就被切成一行一行，这是这个词最实用的画面。

examples.en: A fallen log blocked the path through the forest.
examples.cn: 一段倒下的原木挡住了穿过森林的小路。

examples.en: The pilot logged six hours of flying time that week.
examples.cn: 那名飞行员那一周累计飞行了六个小时。

examples.en: Every visitor is logged at the front desk.
examples.cn: 每位来访者都在前台做了登记。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「烙个」——把每天的事烙在本子上，就成了日志；log 既是木头，也是记录。

root: 来源不确定：中古英语 logge 已指「砍下的木块」，一般认为可能与斯堪的纳维亚语中表示「躺倒的树」的词有关，但没有可靠的拉丁同族词。

sensesIntro.en: The concrete sense is a cut trunk; the record sense grew from sailors writing down what a floating chip told them, and from there the word covers any systematic account.
sensesIntro.cn: 具体的义项是砍下的树干；记录义从船员把浮木读出的数字写下来开始，再扩展到任何系统化的记载。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: an axe bites into a trunk and the cut block falls away.
core.cn: 核心意象：斧头咬进树干，砍下的一截木块滚落在地。

branches.en: walls of a cabin stacked from rough trunks
branches.cn: 用粗原木垒起的小屋墙壁

branches.en: a fire fed with split wood at dusk
branches.cn: 傍晚添进火里的劈柴

branches.en: a captain writing by lamplight on a rolling ship
branches.cn: 船长在摇晃的船上就着灯写日志

branches.en: a radio message copied onto a ruled page
branches.cn: 把无线电消息抄进划好格的一页

branches.en: a milometer turning past a million
branches.cn: 里程表转过一百万的刻度

intro.en: The word is held together by a Middle English noun for a block of wood and a small set of English compounds and suffixes that build its family.
intro.cn: 这个词由中古英语表示「木块」的名词，以及一小套构成其词族的英语复合词和词缀共同支撑。

latinIntro.en: No reliable Latin cognate is recorded; the word is often linked to Scandinavian forms for a fallen tree, but the origin remains uncertain.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有可靠的拉丁同族词；一般认为它与斯堪的纳维亚语中表示「倒下的树」的词有关，但来源仍不确定。

items.meaning: a cut piece of tree; a record book
log plus book, a book of records
items.meaningCN: log 与 book 复合，记录簿

items.meaning: one who cuts timber or keeps records
work held back and not yet done

definition_zh: 变化；变动；使不同；各不相同；（随情况）改变
definition_en: to change, or to differ from one another
core_image: 同一把尺子量十个人，每量一次读数都不一样
scene: 山脚下是春天的花，爬到半山就只见残雪，山顶则冻得人发抖。 Prices vary from shop to shop along the same street.
sceneCN: 这里 vary 是「各不相同、有差异」（第 2 个义项：彼此不同）；句意为同一条街上各家店铺的价格各不相同。尺子每次读数都不一样，就是这个词的样子。

pos.zh: 动词：变化、变动；使不同；各不相同

derivatives.zh: 形容词，义为「各种各样的」
形容词或名词，义为「可变的、变量」
形容词，义为「多样的、各不相同的」

senses.title: To change over time
senses.definition: to change in amount, level or form over time
senses.definitionCN: 在数量、水平或形式上随时间改变
senses.example: The water level varies with the season.
senses.exampleCN: 水位随季节变化。
senses.why: Latin variare means to make different; the verb follows whatever the changing thing does.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 variare 意为使不同；这个动词跟着变化者一起走。

senses.title: To differ from one another
senses.definition: to be different between individual cases
senses.definitionCN: 在各个个体之间有所不同
senses.example: Prices vary from shop to shop along the same street.
senses.exampleCN: 同一条街上各家店铺的价格各不相同。
senses.why: Here nothing changes over time; the differences exist side by side in one moment.
senses.whyCN: 这里没有随时间而变化，差别在同一时刻并排存在。

senses.title: To change deliberately
senses.titleCN: 主动改变：故意换个做法
senses.definition: to make something different on purpose
senses.definitionCN: 有意使某物不同
senses.example: He never varies his route to work.
senses.exampleCN: 他上班路线从不改变。
senses.why: The subject is a person here, and the change is a choice rather than a natural drift.
senses.whyCN: 这里的主语是人，变化是一种选择而不是自然漂移。

senses.title: To depend on something
senses.titleCN: 随……而变：跟着另一个因素走
senses.definition: to change according to another factor
senses.definitionCN: 随另一个因素改变
senses.example: Crop yields vary according to rainfall and soil.
senses.exampleCN: 作物产量随降雨与土壤而变化。
senses.why: The verb leaves the subject to someone else: yields follow the rain, and the rain decides.
senses.whyCN: 这个动词把主导权交给别人：产量跟着雨水走，由雨水决定。

intro.en: Vary is the direct Latin verb variare, to make different, taken into English without an ending change.
intro.cn: vary 就是拉丁语动词 variare「使不同」几乎原样进入英语。

items.en: The adjective varius meant spotted, mixed or of several kinds.
items.cn: 形容词 varius 意为斑驳的、混杂的、多种多样的。

items.en: The verb variare meant to make different, to alternate or to diversify.
items.cn: 动词 variare 意为使不同、交替变换、使多样化。

items.en: Old French variier softened the Latin verb and gave it a French shape.
items.cn: 古法语 variier 让拉丁动词软化，并赋予它法语形态。

items.en: English shortened it to vary in the fourteenth century, meaning to undergo change.
items.cn: 英语在十四世纪把它缩短为 vary，意为经历变化。

items.en: Modern English uses it both for changing and for differing, two sides of one Latin idea.
items.cn: 现代英语既用它表「变化」也表「不同」，这是同一个拉丁观念的两面。

note.en: The look-alike group follows the vari- family; the near-meaning group holds verbs of shifting and differing.
note.cn: 形近组沿 vari- 家族；近义组收表示变化与不同的动词。

entries.definition: Of many kinds, the adjective of the same stem.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「各种各样的」，同词干。

entries.definition: Many kinds or one kind; the noun of the same stem.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「多样性、种类」，同词干。

entries.definition: Something that changes, or a symbol for it.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词或名词，义为「可变的、变量」。

entries.definition: A change or difference in amount or form.
The plain verb for becoming different.
To be unlike, only the side of comparison.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「不同」，只表示比较的一面。

entries.definition: To rise and fall again and again, like a level.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「波动」，反复起落。

entries.definition: To move from one position or state to another.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「转移」，从一个位置或状态移到另一个。

normalIntro.en: The hooks use the two faces of vary, changing and differing, with real phrases from news and shops.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子使用 vary 变化与不同这两面，搭配取自新闻与店铺的真实说法。

normal.en: Vary with time, differ from place to place: one word for both.
normal.cn: 随时间变叫 vary，各地不同也叫 vary：一个词两面用。

normal.en: Prices vary widely means the range is large.
normal.cn: prices vary widely 指差价范围很大。

normal.en: Vary in size means the sizes are not all the same.
normal.cn: vary in size 指大小并不一样。

normal.en: Opinions vary is a polite way of saying nobody agrees.
normal.cn: opinions vary 是「谁都不一致」的礼貌说法。

normal.en: Varied is the adjective, variety the noun, varying the participle.
normal.cn: varied 是形容词，variety 是名词，varying 是分词。

abstract.en: Vary needs two reference points: a thing at two times, or two things at one time.
abstract.cn: vary 需要两个参照点：一样东西的两个时刻，或同一时刻的两样东西。

abstract.en: Change is motion, difference is structure; vary describes both with one shape.
abstract.cn: 变化是运动，差异是结构；vary 用一个形状描述两者。

abstract.en: A life without vary is a line, not a landscape.
abstract.cn: 没有变化的生活是一条线，不是一片风景。

examples.en: Prices vary widely between the two markets.
examples.cn: 两个市场的价格差别很大。

examples.en: Her mood varies with the weather.
examples.cn: 她的心情随天气变化。

examples.en: The recipes vary only in the amount of sugar used.
examples.cn: 这些食谱只是在用糖量上不同。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「威瑞」——威（风）瑞（雨）一来，天气就变：变化

root: 直接来自拉丁语动词 variare「使不同、变换」，经古法语 variier 于十四世纪进入英语；同族词有 various、variety、variable、variation。

sensesIntro.en: Vary covers change over time, difference between cases, deliberate change and dependence on a factor.
sensesIntro.cn: vary 涵盖随时间变化、个体间差异、主动改变与随因素而变四种情形。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one ruler measuring ten people, with ten different readings.
core.cn: 核心意象：一把尺子量十个人，十次读数都不同。

branches.en: TIME LINE: the same thing is different later.
branches.cn: 时间线：同一样东西后来不同了。

branches.en: SPACE LINE: different cases at one moment.
branches.cn: 空间线：同一时刻的各个个体不同。

branches.en: WILL LINE: a person chooses to change.
branches.cn: 意志线：人主动选择改变。

branches.en: CAUSE LINE: one factor pulls another along.
branches.cn: 因果线：一个因素带着另一个走。

branches.en: CONTRAST: change is one thing twice, vary also covers two things once.
branches.cn: 对照线：变化是一样东西的两次，vary 也含两样东西的一次。

intro.en: Vary is a bare Latin verb stem; its English relatives come from adding endings to the same root.
intro.cn: vary 是不带前缀的拉丁动词词干，英语亲属词都在同一词根上加词尾。

latinIntro.en: The Latin base is variare from varius; the English verb drops the ending entirely.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语基础是出自 varius 的 variare，英语动词整个去掉了词尾。

items.example: It forms varied and the past tense.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 varied 与过去式。

items.example: It is shared by the whole family.

definition_en: to build something by putting parts together, or to form an idea in the mind
core_image: 工人把钢梁一根根吊起，拼成桥的骨架
scene: 工地上的吊车正把钢梁送到桥墩上。 Workers construct the bridge in sections.
sceneCN: 这里 construct 指「建造」（第 1 个义项：把材料拼成建筑物）；句意是工人们分段建造这座桥。

senses.title: Build from parts
senses.definition: to build a physical thing by joining materials together
senses.definitionCN: 把材料连接起来建成实物
senses.example: They plan to construct a new school here.
senses.exampleCN: 他们计划在这里建一所新学校。
senses.why: Nothing large appears at once; it is lifted piece by piece.
senses.whyCN: 庞大的东西不会一下出现，而是一块块吊起来。

senses.title: Build in the mind
senses.definition: to form an idea, theory or sentence out of separate parts
senses.definitionCN: 用分散的部分搭出想法、理论或句子
senses.example: She constructed a clear argument from three facts.
senses.exampleCN: 她用三件事实构建了一个清晰的论证。
senses.why: Thought also needs a frame before it can stand.
senses.whyCN: 想法也要先有个架子，才能立起来。

senses.title: Draw by rule
senses.definition: to draw a geometric figure exactly as the rules require
senses.definitionCN: 严格按规则画出几何图形
senses.example: Construct a triangle with these two sides.
senses.exampleCN: 用这两条边作一个三角形。
senses.why: Geometry builds shapes with a ruler and a compass.
senses.whyCN: 几何用尺和圆规把图形搭建出来。

intro.en: Construct comes from Latin construere, to pile up or build, built from com-, together, and struere, to pile.
intro.cn: construct 来自拉丁语 construere，意为堆起或建造，由 com-（一起）与 struere（堆积）构成。

items.en: Struere meant to pile things in layers.
items.cn: struere 意为把东西一层层堆起。

items.en: Construere meant to pile materials into a building.
items.cn: construere 意为把材料堆成一座建筑。

items.en: It also described putting words together in order.
items.cn: 它也描述把词语按顺序组合起来。

items.en: French construire kept both the building and the wording senses.
items.cn: 法语 construire 同时保留建造与组句两层意思。

items.en: English construct meant to build up a structure.
items.cn: 英语 construct 指搭起一座结构。

items.en: It now also covers building an argument or a theory.
items.cn: 如今它也指构建论证或理论。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the Latin pile base struct-, and the meaning group names other verbs for putting a thing together.
note.cn: 形近组共享拉丁语堆积词基 struct-，近义组列出其他表示把事物搭起来的动词。

entries.definition: the process of building something
helpful and intended to improve something
to teach or give an order
to make something by joining parts
to raise a structure into an upright position
to fit separate pieces into one unit

normalIntro.en: These hooks start from steel beams lifted into place, then move to an argument built from facts and to a shape drawn by rule.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子从被吊到位的钢梁开始，再到用事实搭起的论证，最后到按规则画出的图形。

normal.en: Con- is together and struct is pile, so construct is piling pieces into one thing.
normal.cn: con- 是一起，struct 是堆，construct 就是把部件堆成一个东西。

normal.en: A bridge is only a plan until the first beam is hung.
normal.cn: 在第一根梁吊起之前，桥还只是图纸。

normal.en: Sentences are constructed the same way bridges are: part by part.
normal.cn: 句子和桥一样，都是逐件搭起来的。

normal.en: A good argument is built, not shouted.
normal.cn: 好的论证是搭出来的，不是喊出来的。

normal.en: Ask what holds it up, and you will see how it was constructed.
normal.cn: 问它靠什么撑住，你就看出它是怎么建成的。

abstract.en: Picture a crane lowering one long beam.
abstract.cn: 想象一台吊车放下一根长梁。

abstract.en: Picture three blocks stacked into a neat tower.
abstract.cn: 想象三块积木叠成一座整齐的塔。

abstract.en: Picture a compass drawing an exact triangle.
abstract.cn: 想象一把圆规画出一个精确的三角形。

examples.en: Engineers will construct the tunnel in two stages.
examples.cn: 工程师将分两个阶段建造这条隧道。

examples.en: He constructed his answer carefully from the data.
examples.cn: 他依据数据仔细构建了自己的回答。

examples.en: The shelter was constructed of wood and stone.
examples.cn: 这个避难所是用木材和石头建造的。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 construct 记成 con（一起）加 struct（堆积）：把材料一起堆叠搭起来，就是建造。

root: 源自拉丁语 construere（com 一起 + struere 堆积），本义是把材料堆叠起来建成屋宇，后指建造、组句与构想。

sensesIntro.en: From beams lifted into a bridge, to an argument built from facts, and to a triangle drawn with care.
sensesIntro.cn: 从吊成桥梁的钢梁，到用事实搭起的论证，最后到仔细画出的三角形。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: steel beams hanging from a crane, joining one frame.
core.cn: 核心意象：吊车吊着钢梁，合成一副骨架。

branches.en: The first sense is physical joining, beam against beam.
branches.cn: 第一个义项是实体上的连接，梁与梁相接。

branches.en: The second sense builds arguments and sentences from smaller pieces.
branches.cn: 第二个义项用小片段搭出论证与句子。

branches.en: The third sense draws a figure by following fixed rules.
branches.cn: 第三个义项按固定规则画出图形。

branches.en: Both senses need a frame before the whole can stand.
branches.cn: 两个义项都需要先有骨架，整体才能立住。

branches.en: A proof and a drawing both grow step by step.
branches.cn: 证明与作图都是一步一步长出来的。

intro.en: Construct is built on Latin con-, together, plus struere, to pile up.
intro.cn: construct 由拉丁语 con-（一起）与 struere（堆积）构成。

latinIntro.en: The Latin pile base struct- also appears in structure, instruct and destruction.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语的堆积词基 struct- 也出现在 structure、instruct 与 destruction 中。

items.meaning: to pile parts into a built thing
the act or process of building

items.exampleCN: 建造方在图纸上签了字。

items.meaning: a thing that has been built
items.example: The structure held in the wind.
items.exampleCN: 这座建筑在风中站住了。

items.example: A coach instructed the new players.
items.exampleCN: 一位教练指导了新队员。

items.meaning: to pile something in the way
items.example: A fallen tree obstructed the path.
items.exampleCN: 一棵倒下的树挡住了小路。

items.meaning: the pulling down of a built thing
items.exampleCN: 暴风雨造成了大范围的毁坏。

definition_en: to remove something unwanted
core_image: 一只抖落雨水的狗，水珠四散
scene: 他终于清掉了阁楼里堆积多年的旧箱子。 He finally got rid of the old boxes that had piled up in the attic for years.
sceneCN: 这里 rid 是「清除、摆脱」（第 1 个义项：去掉不想要的东西）；句意：他终于清掉了阁楼里堆积多年的旧箱子。

senses.title: Freeing yourself
senses.definition: to make yourself free of something unwanted
senses.definitionCN: 使自己摆脱不想要的东西
senses.example: She was glad to be rid of the cold.
senses.exampleCN: 她很庆幸感冒好了。
senses.why: The word means to clear away what troubles you.
senses.whyCN: 这个词意为清除困扰你的东西。

senses.title: Removing an object
senses.definition: to remove a thing that is no longer wanted
senses.definitionCN: 把不再需要的东西移走
senses.example: We rid the garden of weeds.
senses.exampleCN: 我们清除了花园里的杂草。
senses.why: The same act applies to things as well as feelings.
senses.whyCN: 同样的行为也适用于物品和感受。

senses.title: In get rid of
senses.definition: used in get rid of to mean discard
senses.definitionCN: 用于 get rid of，表示丢弃
senses.example: He got rid of his old bicycle.
senses.exampleCN: 他把旧自行车处理掉了。
senses.why: The fixed phrase keeps the word alive in daily speech.
senses.whyCN: 这个固定短语让这个词在日常口语中保持活力。

intro.en: Rid comes from Old Norse ryðja, to clear land.
intro.cn: rid 源自古诺尔斯语 ryðja（清理土地）。

items.en: Ryðja means to clear land.
items.cn: ryðja 意为清理土地。

items.en: The word enters northern English speech.
items.cn: 这个词进入英格兰北部的语言。

items.en: Rid first means to clear a place.
items.cn: rid 最初指清理一个地方。

items.en: It extends to clearing away unwanted things.
items.cn: 它延伸到清除不想要的东西。

items.en: The phrase get rid of is very common.
items.cn: 短语 get rid of 非常常用。

note.en: Rid means to clear away; remove is the general word.
note.cn: rid 意为清除；remove 是更通用的词。

normalIntro.en: Rid is sweeping the floor until nothing unwanted remains.
normalIntro.cn: rid 是把地扫到不留一点多余之物的动作。

normal.en: Get rid of means throw away or free yourself.
normal.cn: get rid of 意为扔掉或摆脱。

normal.en: Be rid of a cold means no longer have it.

normal.en: Rid the room of dust means clean it.
normal.cn: rid the room of dust 意为打扫房间。

normal.en: Rid oneself of fear means overcome it.
normal.cn: rid oneself of fear 意为克服恐惧。

normal.en: Compare remove: remove is neutral, rid implies something unwanted.
normal.cn: 对比 remove：remove 是中性的，rid 暗含不想要的东西。

abstract.en: Picture a dog shaking rain from its fur.
abstract.cn: 想象一只狗抖落毛上的雨水。

abstract.en: Imagine an attic emptied of old boxes.
abstract.cn: 想象清空了旧箱子的阁楼。

abstract.en: Think of a window opened to let smoke out.
abstract.cn: 想象打开窗户让烟散出去。

examples.en: We must get rid of this old sofa.
examples.cn: 我们必须处理掉这张旧沙发。

examples.en: She was rid of the headache by noon.
examples.cn: 到中午她的头痛就好了。

examples.en: They rid the field of stones.
examples.cn: 他们清除了田里的石头。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「rid」短得像一声「去掉」——一挥手，不想要的东西就没了。

root: 古诺尔斯语 ryðja（清理土地）→ 中古英语 ridden → rid，核心义「清除、使摆脱」。

sensesIntro.en: Rid means to free yourself of something unwanted, to clear objects away, and to discard in the fixed phrase get rid of.
sensesIntro.cn: rid 指摆脱不想要的东西、清除物品，以及在固定短语 get rid of 中表示丢弃。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a dog shaking rainwater from its fur.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只抖落雨水的狗。

branches.en: Freeing yourself is the core sense.
branches.cn: 使自己摆脱是核心含义。

branches.en: Objects can be cleared away too.
branches.cn: 物品也能被清除。

branches.en: The fixed phrase names discarding.
branches.cn: 固定短语表示丢弃。

branches.en: Feelings and objects are both cleared.
branches.cn: 感受与物品都能被清除。

branches.en: Emotional and physical clearing share the phrase.
branches.cn: 情感与实物的清除共用这一短语。

intro.en: Rid comes from Old Norse and has few English affixes.
intro.cn: rid 来自古诺尔斯语，英语中很少再加词缀。

latinIntro.en: It has no Latin root; Old Norse ryðja is the source.
latinIntro.cn: 它没有拉丁词根；古诺尔斯语 ryðja 是来源。
