definition_zh: 帮助；援助；辅助工具；援助物资；援助款；帮助、援助（动词）；有助于
definition_en: help or support given to a person or a cause, or a device that makes a task easier; as a verb, to help someone or make something easier
core_image: 伸过去的一只手，替对方分担一部分重量
scene: 洪水退去后，仓库门口堆满各地送来的纸箱，志愿者正低头登记清单。 Relief workers handed out food aid to families whose homes had been flooded.
sceneCN: 这里 aid 是「援助物资」（第 3 个义项：送往受灾地区的钱物）；句意为救援人员向房屋被淹的家庭发放食品援助。画面里是仓库、纸箱与登记清单的志愿者。

pos.zh: 名词：帮助；援助；辅助器具；援助物资

derivatives.zh: 与 aid 同源的借词，由法语加 -e 的形式而来，义为「助手、随员」
由 aid 加 -ed 构成，义为「有辅助的」，多用于 computer-aided 这类复合词
由 un- 加 aided 构成，义为「无外界帮助的、独立完成的」

senses.title: Help given to someone in need
senses.definition: help or support given to a person, group or cause that needs it
senses.definitionCN: 给予需要帮助的人、群体或事业的帮助与支持
senses.example: The stranded climbers called for aid as soon as the storm eased.
senses.exampleCN: 风暴一减弱，受困的登山者就呼救求援。
senses.why: Latin adiutare is built from ad- 'to' plus iuvare 'to give strength', so aid is literally strength added to someone else.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 adiutare 由 ad-「向」加 iuvare「给予力量」构成，所以援助就是把力量加到对方身上，这正是「分担重量」那只手的意思。

senses.title: A device that makes a task easier
senses.definition: an object or piece of equipment that helps a person do something they could not do easily alone
senses.definitionCN: 帮助人完成难以独立完成之事的物件或设备
senses.example: A simple walking aid helped him cross the room after surgery.
senses.exampleCN: 术后一副简单的助行器帮他走过了房间。
senses.why: The same added strength is turned into a thing you can hold: a hearing aid or a walking aid supplies the missing force in solid form.
senses.whyCN: 同一份「加上的力量」被做成可以握在手里的东西：助听器、助行架就是把这股缺的力气变成了实体。

senses.title: Money and supplies sent to a region
senses.definition: money, food, medicine or equipment sent to a place or group that urgently needs it
senses.definitionCN: 送往急需帮助的地区或群体的钱、食物、药品或设备
senses.example: Trucks carrying medical aid reached the border before dawn.
senses.exampleCN: 运载医疗援助物资的卡车在黎明前抵达边境。
senses.why: Help that can be packed and shipped becomes countable goods, so the abstract noun turns into crates with labels on them.
senses.whyCN: 能被打包运走的帮助成了可清点的货物，于是这个抽象名词变成了贴着标签的一只只箱子。

senses.title: To help a person or group
senses.definition: to help a person or group do something, especially in a difficult situation
senses.definitionCN: 帮助某人或某群体做某事，尤指在困难处境中
senses.example: Volunteers aided the rescue teams in searching the rubble.
senses.exampleCN: 志愿者协助救援队在废墟中搜寻。
senses.why: The verb puts the noun back into motion: the reaching hand is no longer a thing but an act performed on someone's behalf.
senses.whyCN: 动词把名词重新变成动作：那只伸出的手不再是一件东西，而是替别人做出来的一下举动。

senses.title: To make a process easier
senses.definition: to make a process or result easier or more likely to happen
senses.definitionCN: 使某个过程或结果更容易发生、更可能实现
senses.example: Regular exercise aids recovery after a long illness.
senses.exampleCN: 规律运动有助于久病之后的康复。
senses.why: The one helped is no longer a person but a process; adding strength to digestion or recovery is still the same image, with the body's own work as the receiver.
senses.whyCN: 被帮助的对象从人变成了过程；给消化或康复添一把力，仍是同一个画面，只是接受这股力的是身体自己的运转。

intro.en: Aid reached English from Latin through Old French, and the Latin verb behind it literally means to add strength to someone.
intro.cn: aid 经由古法语来自拉丁语，它背后的拉丁动词字面意思就是「把力量加到某人身上」。

items.en: Iuvare meant 'to help, assist, give pleasure or strength'. It is the simple verb at the base of the family.
items.cn: iuvare 意为「帮助、支援、给予力量或愉悦」，是这一词族最底层的简单动词。

items.en: Ad- 'to' plus iuvare produced adiuvare 'to help'; its frequentative adiutare meant 'to keep helping, lend regular assistance'.
items.cn: ad-「向」加 iuvare 构成 adiuvare「帮助」；其反复动词 adiutare 意为「不断帮助、经常援手」。

items.en: The noun adiutorium meant 'help, assistance', and adiutor meant 'a helper'; both show how early the word could name a person and a thing.
items.cn: 名词 adiutorium 意为「帮助、援助」，adiutor 意为「帮手」；两者都说明这个词很早就能指人也指物。

items.en: Old French aide, from the Latin verb, carried the sense of help and assistance into English after the Norman period.
items.cn: 古法语 aide 源自上述拉丁动词，在诺曼征服之后把「帮助、援助」的意思带入英语。

items.en: English kept aid for help, devices and relief, and borrowed aide again from French for a person who assists; the two spellings now divide the work.
items.cn: 英语把 aid 留给「帮助、器具、救援物资」，又再次从法语借入 aide 专指「助手」；两种拼写如今分工明确。

note.en: The first group is made of words that share the spelling or the Latin help-root; the second group is made of words that also mean giving help or relief.
note.cn: 第一组是同拼写或同「帮助」词根的词；第二组是同样表示给予帮助或救济的词。

entries.definition: A person who helps someone important, such as an assistant to a politician; same sound, but it names a human being.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「助手、随员」，如政界人士的助理；读音相同，但专指人。

entries.definition: The past form and participle of the verb, or an adjective in compounds such as computer-aided.
entries.definitionCN: 动词的过去式与过去分词，也可作形容词用于 computer-aided 一类复合词。

entries.definition: Without help from anyone or anything; formed with the negative prefix un-.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「无外界帮助的」，由否定前缀 un- 加 aided 构成。

entries.definition: The name of a disease, formed from the initials of its full medical name; it merely looks similar and comes from another source.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，指一种免疫缺陷疾病，由其医学全称的首字母构成；只是拼写相近，词源不同。

entries.definition: The everyday word for making things easier for someone; broader and less formal than aid.
entries.definitionCN: 动词或名词，义为「帮助」，是最日常的说法，范围比 aid 宽，语气也更随意。

entries.definition: To help, usually as a secondary partner rather than the main agent; more formal than help.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「协助」，通常指作为次要一方参与，而非主导者，比 help 正式。

entries.definition: To hold up or back someone over time, financially or emotionally; longer-term than a single act of aid.
entries.definitionCN: 动词或名词，义为「支持、支撑」，可指长期的经济或情感支撑，比一次性的 aid 更持久。

entries.definition: Help given to people in disaster or poverty, often as food, money or shelter; the usual word for emergency aid.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「救济、救援」，多指灾荒中提供的食物、钱款或住所，是紧急援助的常用词。

entries.definition: Money paid by a government to lower a price or support an industry; a narrow, financial kind of aid.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「补贴、补助金」，指政府为压低价格或扶持行业而支付的款项，是 aid 中偏财政的一种。

normalIntro.en: The hooks here follow the real Latin verb and the fixed phrases the word appears in.
normalIntro.cn: 这里的钩子顺着真实的拉丁动词，以及这个词实际出现的固定搭配。

normal.en: Ad- means to, iuvare means give strength: aid is strength handed over to somebody.
normal.cn: ad- 是「向」，iuvare 是「给力量」：aid 就是把力量递到别人手上。

normal.en: The frequentative adiutare adds the idea of repeated help, not one dramatic rescue.
normal.cn: 反复动词 adiutare 带出「反复帮助」的意思，而不是一次戏剧性的营救。

normal.en: First aid is the help given before any doctor arrives.
normal.cn: first aid 是医生到来之前给的那份帮助。

normal.en: A hearing aid adds strength to a sense that has grown weak.
normal.cn: hearing aid 是给变弱的感官补上力气。

normal.en: Aid is the help itself, while aide is the person who gives it.
normal.cn: aid 是帮助本身，aide 则是提供帮助的那个人。

abstract.en: Picture two people carrying one heavy crate: the second pair of hands takes part of the weight without taking the crate away.
abstract.cn: 想象两个人抬一只很重的箱子：后来那双手分走了一部分重量，却没有把箱子整个接过去。

abstract.en: The same hands can become a walking frame, a box of medicine or a cheque: the shape changes, the added strength does not.
abstract.cn: 同一双手可以变成助行架、一箱药或一张支票：形状变了，补上的那股力气没变。

abstract.en: Aid does not do the whole job for you; it makes the job possible for you to finish.
abstract.cn: 援助并不替你把整件事做完，它只是让你有能力把它做完。

examples.en: The old map was a great aid to us in the dark forest.
examples.cn: 在那片漆黑的森林里，那张旧地图给了我们很大帮助。

examples.en: Several countries sent aid after the earthquake.
examples.cn: 地震之后，几个国家送来了援助物资。

examples.en: A gentle stretch can aid sleep after a long flight.
examples.cn: 长途飞行后做些轻柔的拉伸有助于睡眠。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「诶的」——一只手递过去，对方应了一声「诶」，援助就到了

root: 拉丁语 adiuvare「帮助」由 ad-「向」加 iuvare「给予力量」构成，其反复动词 adiutare 意为「不断帮助」；名词 adiutorium「援助」经古法语 aide 进入英语，成为 aid。

sensesIntro.en: Five senses all carry one image, strength added to someone else's load: the help itself, the tool that supplies it, the goods that carry it, the act of giving it, and the process it makes easier.
sensesIntro.cn: 五个义项共用同一个画面——把力量加到别人的负担上：帮助本身、提供这份力量的器具、把帮助装运出去的物资、给出帮助的动作，以及被这份力量推动得更顺的过程。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a second pair of hands takes part of the weight without taking the whole load.
core.cn: 核心意象：多出来的一双手分走一部分重量，却不把整副担子接走。

branches.en: THE PERSON: help given to someone who cannot carry the load alone.
branches.cn: 人的一线：给予无法独自承担之人的那份帮助。

branches.en: THE OBJECT: the added strength is built into a hearing aid or a walking aid.
branches.cn: 器物的一线：补上的力气被做成助听器或助行架。

branches.en: THE CARGO: help that can be packed becomes countable aid on a truck.
branches.cn: 货物的一线：能装箱的帮助成了卡车上一件件可清点的援助物资。

branches.en: THE ACT: the verb names the moment of reaching out, not the thing handed over.
branches.cn: 动作的一线：动词说的是伸手那一刻，而不是递过去的东西。

branches.en: THE PROCESS: when the receiver is digestion or recovery, the same strength becomes a factor that helps things along.
branches.cn: 过程的一线：当接受者是消化或康复时，同一股力气就成了推动事情顺利进行的因素。

intro.en: Aid comes in as a whole French word, but Latin prefixes and English suffixes organise its family.
intro.cn: aid 是作为完整的法语词进入英语的，但拉丁前缀与英语后缀把这个词族组织了起来。

latinIntro.en: The Latin verbs adiuvare and adiutare, the noun adiutorium and the agent noun adiutor are all attested, so only the deeper Indo-European layer is reconstruction.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语动词 adiuvare、adiutare，名词 adiutorium 与施事名词 adiutor 均有文献记录，只有更深的印欧语层次属于重构。

items.example: It marks the direction of the help in adiuvare.
items.exampleCN: 在 adiuvare 里，这个前缀标出帮助所朝的方向。

items.example: The verb is the semantic core of the family.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词是这一词族的语义核心。

items.example: The repeated action is marked by the suffix -tare.
items.exampleCN: 反复的动作由后缀 -tare 标出。

items.example: It entered English from Old French aide.
items.exampleCN: 它经古法语 aide 进入英语。

items.example: It was borrowed again to name a person.
items.exampleCN: 它被再次借入，用来指人。

items.example: It forms aid worker and aid agency.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 aid worker 与 aid agency。

definition_en: as far as one can see or judge; reportedly; seemingly, though not certainly
core_image: 从表面看得出的样子，却给自己留了余地
scene: 清晨的咖啡馆里，店员看了一眼空着的餐台。 Apparently the delivery van broke down on the way.
sceneCN: 这里 apparently 是「看来」（第 1 个义项：根据眼前可见的情况作出判断，但语气留有余地）；句意为「看来送货车在半路上抛锚了」。画面里有清晨的咖啡馆、空着的餐台和望向门外的店员。

pos.zh: 副词：看来；显然；据说；表面上

derivatives.zh: 去掉副词后缀 -ly 得到的形容词，义为「明显的；表面上的」
与本词同出拉丁语 apparere，义为「出现；显得」
同出 apparere 这一词根的名词，义为「出现；外表」

senses.title: As far as one can tell
senses.definition: used to say that something seems to be true from the evidence available, without claiming certainty
senses.definitionCN: 表示根据手头可见的证据，某事看来为真，但不宣称确定
senses.example: Apparently the delivery van broke down on the way.
senses.exampleCN: 看来送货车在半路上抛锚了。
senses.why: The adjective means 'visible'; the adverb says that what is visible is all one has to go on, so the claim is made from the surface only.
senses.whyCN: 形容词义为「可见的」；副词则表示可见的东西就是全部依据，因此这个判断只从表面作出。

senses.title: Reportedly, according to others
senses.definition: used to report what other people say, especially when the speaker cannot confirm it personally
senses.definitionCN: 用于转述别人的说法，尤其是说话人自己无法亲自证实时
senses.example: Apparently the whole street lost power for two hours.
senses.exampleCN: 据说整条街停了两个小时的电。
senses.why: Once 'what appears' can come from hearsay as well as from sight, the adverb becomes a polite way of quoting the town without vouching for it.
senses.whyCN: 当「显现出来的东西」也可以来自传闻而不只是亲眼所见，这个副词就变成一种得体的转述方式，替街坊传话却不作担保。

senses.title: Seemingly, but perhaps not really
senses.definition: used to describe how something looks while hinting that the reality may be different
senses.definitionCN: 用于描述某事物的外观，同时暗示实际情况可能不同
senses.example: She was apparently unaware of the new rule.
senses.exampleCN: 她看来并不知道这条新规定。
senses.why: The word can also warn: if only the surface has been read, the appearance may be a mask rather than the fact.
senses.whyCN: 这个词也能起提醒作用：如果只读了表面，那副样子就可能是面具而不是事实。

senses.title: To soften a statement
senses.definition: used in conversation to make an assertion less direct or less confrontational
senses.definitionCN: 用于谈话中，使断言不那么直接、不那么咄咄逼人
senses.example: Apparently, we are expected to bring our own cups.
senses.exampleCN: 看样子，我们要自己带杯子。
senses.why: By attributing the claim to appearance rather than to oneself, the speaker avoids sounding blunt while still passing the message on.
senses.whyCN: 把断言归给「表面现象」而不是归给自己，说话人既能不显得生硬，又把话传了出去。

intro.en: Apparently is the adverb of apparent, built on a Latin verb meaning 'come into sight' plus the native suffix -ly.
intro.cn: apparently 是 apparent 的副词形式，由表示「进入视野」的拉丁动词加上本族后缀 -ly 构成。

items.en: Apparere 'come into view' is built from ad- 'to' and parere 'come forth'; its participle apparans yields the adjective.
items.cn: apparere「进入视野」由 ad-「向」与 parere「出现」构成；它的分词 apparans 给出了形容词。

items.en: The participle aparant passes into English as apparent, and English later adds its own adverb suffix.
items.cn: 分词 aparant 作为 apparent 进入英语，英语后来又给它加上自己的副词后缀。

items.en: Apparently is recorded first in the sense 'evidently, plainly', close to the adjective's 'visible' sense.
items.cn: apparently 最初有记载的义项是「明显地、明白地」，接近形容词「可见的」义。

items.en: The reporting sense 'so people say' becomes common in newspapers and conversation.
items.cn: 转述义「听人说」在报纸与谈话中变得常见。

items.en: The adverb now mostly hedges: it presents a claim as seeming rather than certain, and often softens the sentence.
items.cn: 现代这个副词主要起留余地的作用：把断言呈现为「看来」而非确定，并常用来缓和语气。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the family from the same Latin verb; the near-meaning group gathers adverbs that hedge or report.
note.cn: 形近组收同出那个拉丁动词的一族词；近义组收表示留余地或转述的副词。

entries.definition: The adjective meaning clearly visible or merely seeming.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「明显的」或「表面上的」，本词由它加 -ly 构成。

entries.definition: A verb meaning to come into sight or to seem.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「出现；显得」，与本词同根。

entries.definition: A noun meaning the act of appearing or the outward look.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「出现；外表」，与本词同根。

entries.definition: A noun meaning a ghostly figure that appears.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「幽灵、幻影」，同出此词根。

entries.definition: Clearly, judging from the evidence.
entries.definitionCN: 根据证据来看显然如此，语气比 apparently 更肯定。

entries.definition: According to what has been reported, not confirmed by the speaker.
entries.definitionCN: 据报导、据传，明确表示来自转述，与 apparently 的「据说」义最近。

entries.definition: As it appears, often with a hint that the appearance may mislead.
entries.definitionCN: 看来如此，常暗示表象可能误导，与 apparently 的「表面上」义接近。

entries.definition: According to outward claim, often with doubt implied.
entries.definitionCN: 据对外宣称如此，常暗含怀疑，比 apparently 更强调「名义上」。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the real 'visible' root and the hedging positions the adverb takes in a sentence.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些钩子使用真实的「可见」词根，以及这个副词在句中留余地时的位置。

normal.en: The adjective means 'visible'; the adverb says that is all you have to go on.
normal.cn: 形容词义为「可见的」；副词则说这就是你手里的全部依据。

normal.en: Put it at the front to report: apparently, the van broke down.
normal.cn: 放在句首表示转述：看来，送货车抛锚了。

normal.en: It hedges a claim without denying it: apparently safe, but check first.
normal.cn: 它给断言留余地却不否认：看来安全，但先核实一下。

normal.en: It also softens: apparently, we need our own cups.
normal.cn: 它还能缓和语气：看样子，我们要自己带杯子。

normal.en: The family is regular: apparent, appear, appearance, apparition.
normal.cn: 这一族很规整：apparent、appear、appearance、apparition。

abstract.en: Picture a surface catching light while the depths below stay dark.
abstract.cn: 想象一个表面被光照亮，而下方的深处仍然发暗。

abstract.en: The word is a hand pointing at what is seen, with the other hand raised in caution.
abstract.cn: 这个词是一只手指出所见之物，另一只手同时抬起表示谨慎。

abstract.en: It keeps a door open: the sentence can always be revised when facts arrive.
abstract.cn: 它留着一扇门：等事实到来时，这句话随时可以修正。

examples.en: Apparently the delivery van broke down on the way.
examples.cn: 看来送货车在半路上抛锚了。

examples.en: She was apparently unaware of the new rule.
examples.cn: 她看来并不知道这条新规定。

examples.en: The path is apparently safe, though the map is old.
examples.cn: 这条路看来是安全的，尽管地图已经很旧。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「额怕认特利」——餐台空了，店员说「特地利索地送来了？看来没有」：看来

root: apparently 由 apparent 加本族副词后缀 -ly 构成，而 apparent 经古法语 aparant 来自拉丁语 apparere「进入视野、显现」，该动词由 ad-「向」与 parere「出现、可见」构成。十六世纪最初义为「明显地」；十九世纪在报纸与谈话中发展出「据说」的转述义；现代主要用来留余地，把断言呈现为「看来」而非确定。

sensesIntro.en: Four uses fan out from the surface of what is seen: a judgment from available evidence, a report from others, a warning that appearance may deceive, and a conversational softener.
sensesIntro.cn: 四个用法从所见之物的表面展开：根据现有证据的判断、转述他人的说法、提醒表象可能骗人，以及谈话中的缓和用法。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a lit surface above dark depths, read with one hand raised in caution.
core.cn: 核心意象：深处黑暗之上的一片受光表面，一只手边读边抬起示警。

chain: AS FAR AS ONE CAN TELL

branches.en: THE SURFACE LINE: the conclusion is drawn from what can be seen.
branches.cn: 表面线：结论取自看得见的部分。

branches.en: THE REPORT LINE: the evidence is what other people say.
branches.cn: 转述线：证据来自别人所说的话。

branches.en: THE WARNING LINE: appearance may be a mask, not the fact.
branches.cn: 警示线：表象可能是面具，而不是事实。

branches.en: THE SOFTENER LINE: the claim is passed on without a hard edge.
branches.cn: 缓和线：断言被传出去，却不带坚硬的棱角。

branches.en: THE HEDGE LINE: both hearsay and appearance keep certainty at arm's length.
branches.cn: 留余地线：传闻与表象都把确定性挡在一臂之外。

intro.en: Apparently is a hybrid: a Latin-rooted adjective plus the native English adverb suffix -ly.
intro.cn: apparently 是混合体：拉丁词根的形容词加上本族英语副词后缀 -ly。

latinIntro.en: The Latin layer is genuine: apparere is the verb behind the adjective, and parere sits inside that verb.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁层是真实的：apparere 是形容词背后的动词，而 parere 又嵌在那个动词里。

items.example: Apparently the shop opens late on Mondays.
items.exampleCN: 看来这家店周一开得晚。

items.example: The damage was apparent at once.
It turns the adjective into a manner adverb.
items.exampleCN: 它把形容词变成表示方式的副词。

items.example: The verb is the root of the whole family.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词是整族词的根。

items.example: Parere gives the verb its visible core.
items.exampleCN: parere 提供了动词中「可见」的核心。

items.example: Stars appear one by one at dusk.
items.exampleCN: 黄昏时星星一颗颗出现。

items.meaning: the act of appearing; outward look
items.example: His appearance at the door surprised us.
items.exampleCN: 他出现在门口，让我们吃了一惊。
那个幻影在日出时消失了。

items.example: It directs the appearing towards the viewer.

latinEntries.example: Apparere is the direct source of apparent.
latinEntries.exampleCN: apparere 是 apparent 的直接来源。

definition_zh: 连续的；不间断的；连绵的
definition_en: happening or existing without any break or gap
core_image: 一笔画到底的直线，中间没有断口
scene: 印刷机一开就停不下来，纸带一直往外送。 The press produced a continuous sheet of paper.
sceneCN: 这里 continuous 指「不间断的」（第 1 个义项：中间没有中断）；句意是印刷机送出一整条没有断口的纸。

pos.zh: 连续的；不间断的；连绵的

senses.title: Without a break
senses.definition: going on with no pause or gap in time
senses.definitionCN: 在时间上进行中没有任何停顿或缺口
senses.example: A continuous line runs along the top of the page.
senses.exampleCN: 一条不断的线横贯页面顶端。
senses.why: The eye trusts a line that never lifts from the paper.
senses.whyCN: 眼睛信任一条始终没离开纸面的线。

senses.title: Unbroken in space
senses.definition: covering an area from end to end without gaps
senses.definitionCN: 在空间上从头到尾连成一片没有空隙
senses.example: A continuous wall surrounds the old town.
senses.exampleCN: 一道连绵的墙围着老城。
senses.why: No gate and no crack means the wall reads as one thing.
senses.whyCN: 没有门也没有裂缝，墙就读成一个整体。

senses.title: Steady in supply
senses.definition: provided at every moment over a period of time
senses.definitionCN: 在一段时间内每一刻都得到供应
senses.example: The plant needs a continuous supply of cool air.
senses.exampleCN: 这座工厂需要持续的冷气供应。
senses.why: Some processes cannot wait for the next delivery.
senses.whyCN: 有些过程等不到下一批货。

intro.en: Continuous comes from Latin continuus, hanging together without a break, from continere, to hold together.
intro.cn: continuous 来自拉丁语 continuus（连在一起、不断开），源于 continere（保持在一起）。

items.en: Continere meant to keep parts in one unbroken whole.
items.cn: continere 意为把各部分保持在一个不断开的整体里。

items.en: Continuus described a line or period with no gap.
items.cn: continuus 形容没有缺口的线或时段。

items.en: The suffix -ous marked a quality in adjectives.
items.cn: 后缀 -ous 在形容词里表示某种性质。

items.en: French continu carried the same unbroken sense.
items.cn: 法语 continu 带有同样的不断义。

items.en: English continuous was used for time, space and motion.
items.cn: 英语 continuous 用于时间、空间与运动。

items.en: It is now carefully kept apart from continual.
items.cn: 如今它被小心地与 continual 区分开。

note.en: The look-alike group sets continuous against its closest relatives, and the meaning group names other words for what does not break.
note.cn: 形近组把 continuous 与最亲近的几个词放在一起，近义组列出其他表示不断开的词。

entries.definition: happening again and again with short breaks
to keep going after a pause
without a pause at any moment
staying the same and never stopping
not interrupted at any point
regular and not changing

normalIntro.en: These hooks start with a line that never lifts, then move to a wall without a gate and a supply that never waits.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子从始终不抬起的线开始，再到没有门的墙，最后到等不得的供应。

normal.en: Continuous means no gap, while continual means many gaps.
normal.cn: continuous 是没有缺口，continual 是许多缺口。

normal.en: Draw one stroke across the page and do not lift the pen.
normal.cn: 在纸上一笔画过去，不要抬笔。

normal.en: A wall with no gate is continuous, and so is a hum with no pause.
normal.cn: 没有门的墙是不间断的，没有停顿的嗡嗡声也是。

normal.en: Think of a tap that never closes for an hour.
normal.cn: 想一想一只一小时都没关的水龙头。

normal.en: If you can point to a break, the word is not this one.
normal.cn: 只要你能指出一处中断，这个词就不适用。

abstract.en: Picture a single white stroke on a dark page.
abstract.cn: 想象深色纸面上只有一笔白线。

abstract.en: Picture a ribbon pulled tight with no knot.
abstract.cn: 想象一条拉紧、没有打结的丝带。

abstract.en: Picture a river that never shows a dry stone.
abstract.cn: 想象一条从不露出干石的河。

examples.en: The machine needs a continuous supply of water.
examples.cn: 这台机器需要持续供水。

examples.en: A continuous line of cars filled the road.
examples.cn: 一长串不断的车占满了路。

examples.en: The baby slept in a continuous stretch.

definition_en: equal in value, meaning, or effect, or something that matches another
core_image: 两枚不同的硬币放在天平上，重量正好相同
scene: 一英里大约相当于一点六公里。 One mile is roughly equivalent to one point six kilometers.

senses.title: Equal in value or amount
senses.definition: having the same value, amount, or meaning as something else

senses.example: A dollar is not equivalent to a euro.
senses.exampleCN: 一美元并不等于一欧元。

senses.exampleCN: 沉默等同于同意。

senses.why: The adjective becomes a noun for the matching item itself.

dict_mnemonic.text: software 是 soft 与 ware 的组合；software update 是「软件更新」，software engineer 是「软件工程师」。

root: 由 soft（软的）与 ware（货物）组合而成，类比 hardware 造出，指计算机运行的程序。

sensesIntro.en: Software is computer programs, a software product, or the software industry.
sensesIntro.cn: software 指计算机程序、软件产品，或软件业。

core.en: Written instructions that make a machine work.
core.cn: 让机器运转的书面指令。

branches.en: Code tells the machine what to do.
branches.cn: 代码告诉机器做什么。

branches.en: A product is sold in boxes or downloads.
branches.cn: 产品以盒装或下载方式出售。

branches.en: An industry grows around writing code.
branches.cn: 围绕编写代码成长出一个行业。

branches.en: The code and the product made from it share a name.
branches.cn: 代码与由它制成的产品共用一个名称。

branches.en: Products and the people who make them form a field.
branches.cn: 产品与制造产品的人构成一个领域。

intro.en: Software builds words for its engineers, updates, and business.
intro.cn: software 构成表示其工程师、更新和商业的词。

latinIntro.en: Both halves are Germanic: soft from Old English, ware from Old English goods.
latinIntro.cn: 两部分都源于日耳曼语：soft 来自古英语，ware 来自古英语的货物。

items.example: The software engineer wrote the fix.
items.exampleCN: 软件工程师编写了修复程序。

items.exampleCN: 这家软件公司雇了十个人。
